5.2.10.s: aindrāgnena paśūnām̐ vidhir āmnātaḥ /
5.2.10.d: ऐन्द्राग्नेन पशूनाम्̐ विधिर् आम्नातः /
5.2.10.m: By the [procedure] dedicated to Indra and Agni, the rule for animals is taught.

5.2.10.s: varam anādiṣṭadakṣiṇāsu dadyād gāṃ trihāyaṇīṃ caturhāyaṇīm̐ vā /
5.2.10.d: वरम् अनादिष्टदक्षिणासु दद्याद् गां त्रिहायणीं चतुर्हायणीम्̐ वा /
5.2.10.m: In rites where the sacrificial gift is not specified, he should give a boon, or a three-year-old cow, or a four-year-old cow.

5.2.10.s: ijyāsūpām̐śudevatāḥ prajāpatir vāyur devāḥ sūryo 'ditir viṣṇur viṣṇuvaruṇau savitauṣadhayo dyāvāpṛthivī bhūmir yamaś ca /
5.2.10.d: इज्यासूपाम्̐शुदेवताः प्रजापतिर् वायुर् देवाः सूर्यो ऽदितिर् विष्णुर् विष्णुवरुणौ सवितौषधयो द्यावापृथिवी भूमिर् यमश् च /
5.2.10.m: In sacrifices, the whisper deities are: Prajāpati, Vāyu, the Viśve Devas, Sūrya, Aditi, Viṣṇu, Viṣṇu-and-Varuṇa, Savitṛ, the Plants, Heaven-and-Earth, the Earth, and Yama.

5.2.10.s: saumyaṃ babhrum iti prabhṛtayo yamāntāḥ kāmyāḥ paśubandhāḥ / teṣām̐ somo dhenum itiprabhṛtīni yamāntāni ṣaḍ arcāni /
5.2.10.d: सौम्यं बभ्रुम् इति प्रभृतयो यमान्ताः काम्याः पशुबन्धाः / तेषाम्̐ सोमो धेनुम् इतिप्रभृतीनि यमान्तानि षड् अर्चानि /
5.2.10.m: The wish-granting animal sacrifices are those beginning with 'A brown [victim] to Soma' up to those ending with Yama; their six-verse hymns are those beginning with 'Soma, the milch cow…' up to those ending with Yama.

5.2.10.s: karmādhikyam̐ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ /
5.2.10.d: कर्माधिक्यम्̐ व्याख्यास्यामः /
5.2.10.m: We shall explain the addition of ritual acts.

5.2.10.s: yas traitānām uttamo jāyeta tam̐ saumāpauṣṇam ālabheta paśukāmaḥ /
5.2.10.d: यस् त्रैतानाम् उत्तमो जायेत तम्̐ सौमापौष्णम् आलभेत पशुकामः /
5.2.10.m: Whichever is born the last among triplets, that one one who desires cattle should slaughter for Soma and Pūṣan.

5.2.10.s: audumbaro yūpaḥ /
5.2.10.d: औदुम्बरो यूपः /

5.2.10.s: prājāpatyaṃ tūparam ālabheta paśukāmaḥ /
5.2.10.d: प्राजापत्यं तूपरम् आलभेत पशुकामः /
5.2.10.m: One who desires cattle should seize a hornless [goat] for Prajāpati.

5.2.10.s: āghārāprīsāmidhenya āgnicitike vyākhyātāḥ /
5.2.10.d: आघाराप्रीसामिधेन्य आग्निचितिके व्याख्याताः /
5.2.10.m: The butter-libations, āprī-hymns, and sāmidhenī-verses are explained in [the section on] the piling of the fire altar.

5.2.10.s: dakṣiṇākāle hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇā tārpyam adhivāsaś ca /
5.2.10.d: दक्षिणाकाले हिरण्यं दक्षिणा तार्प्यम् अधिवासश् च /
5.2.10.m: At the time of the sacrificial gifts, gold, a woven garment, and an upper cloth are the sacrificial gift.

5.2.10.s: pariharaṇakāle prāśitrasya dvādaśabrahmaudanān paktvā madhyataḥkāribhyo dadyāt tebhyo dvādaśadvādaśa varān dadāti /
5.2.10.d: परिहरणकाले प्राशित्रस्य द्वादशब्रह्मौदनान् पक्त्वा मध्यतःकारिभ्यो दद्यात् तेभ्यो द्वादशद्वादश वरान् ददाति /
5.2.10.m: At the time of carrying around the prāśitra portion, having cooked twelve brahmaudanacarus, he should give [them] to the principal officiating priests; he gives twelve choices [of gifts] to each of them.

5.2.10.s: devebhyo 'vim̐ vaśām ālabhetādityebhyo vā prajākāmaḥ paśukāmaḥ kāmāyakāmāya /
5.2.10.d: देवेभ्यो ऽविम्̐ वशाम् आलभेतादित्येभ्यो वा प्रजाकामः पशुकामः कामायकामाय /
5.2.10.m: One who desires offspring or who desires cattle should seize a barren sheep for the gods, or for the Ādityas, for whatever desire [he may have].

5.2.10.s: malhā gṛṣṭiḥ /
5.2.10.d: मल्हा गृष्टिः /

5.2.10.s: viṣame samaṃ kṛtvā vaiṣṇavam̐ vāmanam ālabheta bhrātṛvyavān /
5.2.10.d: विषमे समं कृत्वा वैष्णवम्̐ वामनम् आलभेत भ्रातृव्यवान् /
5.2.10.m: Having made [the ground] level when it was uneven, one who has rivals should seize a dwarf [bull] for Viṣṇu.

5.2.10.s: yaḥ pāpmanā tamasā gṛhīto manyeta sa etam aindram ṛṣabham ālabhetāgneyaṃ tu pūrvam ajam ālabheta /
5.2.10.d: यः पाप्मना तमसा गृहीतो मन्येत स एतम् ऐन्द्रम् ऋषभम् आलभेताग्नेयं तु पूर्वम् अजम् आलभेत /
5.2.10.m: He who considers himself seized by evil [and] darkness should seize this bull for Indra; but he should first seize a goat for Agni.

5.2.10.s: kṣutpāpmanā tamobhir hataḥ sāvitraṃ punarutsṛṣṭam ālabheta /
5.2.10.d: क्षुत्पाप्मना तमोभिर् हतः सावित्रं पुनरुत्सृष्टम् आलभेत /
5.2.10.m: One stricken by the evil of hunger and by darkness should seize a [bull] let loose again for Savitṛ.

5.2.10.s: oṣadhībhyo vehatam ālabheta prajākāmaḥ /
5.2.10.d: ओषधीभ्यो वेहतम् आलभेत प्रजाकामः /
5.2.10.m: One who desires offspring should seize a cow that miscarries for the Plants.

5.2.10.s: dyāvāpṛthivīye dhenū saṃmātarā ālabhetānnakāmaḥ /
5.2.10.d: द्यावापृथिवीये धेनू संमातरा आलभेतान्नकामः /
5.2.10.m: One who desires food should seize two milch cows having a common mother for Heaven and Earth.

5.2.10.s: śvobhūte vatsam̐ vāyava ālabheta /
5.2.10.d: श्वोभूते वत्सम्̐ वायव आलभेत /
5.2.10.m: On the next day, he should seize a calf for Vāyu.

5.2.10.s: aindrīm̐ sūtavaśām ālabheta rājanyo bhūtikāmaḥ /
5.2.10.d: ऐन्द्रीम्̐ सूतवशाम् आलभेत राजन्यो भूतिकामः /
5.2.10.m: A noble who desires prosperity should seize a barren cow after bearing a calf for Indra.

5.2.10.s: sūtavaśāyāḥ putram aindram ṛṣabham ālabheta tejaskāmaḥ /
5.2.10.d: सूतवशायाः पुत्रम् ऐन्द्रम् ऋषभम् आलभेत तेजस्कामः /
5.2.10.m: One who desires fiery splendour should seize the son of the barren cow after bearing a calf, a bull for Indra.

5.2.10.s: sārasvatīṃ dhenuṣṭarīm ālabhetānusṛṣṭim /
5.2.10.d: सारस्वतीं धेनुष्टरीम् आलभेतानुसृष्टिम् /
5.2.10.m: He should seize a sterile milch cow that has calved after for Sarasvatī.

5.2.10.s: dyāvāpṛthivīyāṃ dhenuṃ paryāriṇīm ālabheta parisṛtvatīm /
5.2.10.d: द्यावापृथिवीयां धेनुं पर्यारिणीम् आलभेत परिसृत्वतीम् /
5.2.10.m: He should seize a cow prone to abortion, running about, for Heaven and Earth.

5.2.10.s: gomṛgam̐ vāyava ālabheta gāṃ mṛgam /
5.2.10.d: गोमृगम्̐ वायव आलभेत गां मृगम् /
5.2.10.m: He should seize a wild ox—a cow-deer—for Vāyu.

5.2.10.s: aindrāgnam anusṛṣṭam ālabheta yasya pitā pitāmahaḥ somaṃ na pibet /
5.2.10.d: ऐन्द्राग्नम् अनुसृष्टम् आलभेत यस्य पिता पितामहः सोमं न पिबेत् /
5.2.10.m: He whose father and grandfather did not drink soma should seize a [beast] born after for Indra and Agni.

5.2.10.s: paṇḍako yatra bhūmer jāyeta tad adhyavasāyeta / saumāpauṣṇaṃ napum̐sakam ālabheta paṇḍakam̐ yājayet /
5.2.10.d: पण्डको यत्र भूमेर् जायेत तद् अध्यवसायेत / सौमापौष्णं नपुम्̐सकम् आलभेत पण्डकम्̐ याजयेत् /
5.2.10.m: Where a eunuch is born of the land, he should settle there; he should seize a gelded [beast] for Soma and Pūṣan [and] make the eunuch sacrifice.

5.2.10.s: prāg ghavirāhuter anavadānīyānām aṅgānāṃ dakṣiṇāprātīco 'ṅgārān upohya nirṛtyai svāhā \\ iti juhoti /
5.2.10.d: प्राग् घविराहुतेर् अनवदानीयानाम् अङ्गानां दक्षिणाप्रातीचो ऽङ्गारान् उपोह्य निरृत्यै स्वाहा \\ इति जुहोति /
5.2.10.m: Before the oblation offering of the parts not to be cut off, having pushed the embers towards the south-west, he offers with: 'To Nirṛti, svāhā!'

5.2.10.s: vāruṇaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ petva ekaśitipāt tenāmayāvī dvīpe yajeta yam̐ samantam āpaḥ parivaheyuḥ /
5.2.10.d: वारुणः कृष्णः पेत्व एकशितिपात् तेनामयावी द्वीपे यजेत यम्̐ समन्तम् आपः परिवहेयुः /
5.2.10.m: A black castrated ram with one white foot is for Varuṇa; with that, a sick man should sacrifice on an island around which waters flow on all sides.

5.2.10.s: sarvakṛṣṇo 'bhicarataḥ /
5.2.10.d: सर्वकृष्णो ऽभिचरतः /
5.2.10.m: An entirely black one is for one who performs sorcery.

5.2.10.s: siddham ā niyojanāt //
5.2.10.d: सिद्धम् आ नियोजनात् //

5.2.10.s: paśuṃ badhnāmi \\ iti niyunakti /
5.2.10.d: पशुं बध्नामि \\ इति नियुनक्ति /
5.2.10.m: He ties [the victim] with: 'I bind the animal.'

5.2.10.s: vaśānām̐ saptamo 'nuvākaḥ /
5.2.10.d: वशानाम्̐ सप्तमो ऽनुवाकः /
5.2.10.m: [This is] the seventh anuvāka, [the section] of the barren cows.

5.2.10.s: ukṣā brāhmaṇaspatyaḥ /
5.2.10.d: उक्षा ब्राह्मणस्पत्यः /

5.2.10.s: kṛṣṇaśabalyāś carma viśasanena jahyāt /
5.2.10.d: कृष्णशबल्याश् चर्म विशसनेन जह्यात् /
5.2.10.m: He should remove the skin of a black-spotted [cow] by dissecting.

5.2.10.s: ṛṣabhāṇām aṣṭamaḥ /
5.2.10.d: ऋषभाणाम् अष्टमः /

5.2.10.s: indrāya vajriṇa ṛṣabham ālabheta rājanyo bhūtikāmaḥ /
5.2.10.d: इन्द्राय वज्रिण ऋषभम् आलभेत राजन्यो भूतिकामः /
5.2.10.m: A noble who desires prosperity should seize a bull for Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt.

5.2.10.s: havirāhutau hūyamānāyām̐ yaṃ dviṣyāt taṃ manasā dhyāyet /
5.2.10.d: हविराहुतौ हूयमानायाम्̐ यं द्विष्यात् तं मनसा ध्यायेत् /
5.2.10.m: While the oblation-offering is being offered, he should meditate in his mind on him whom he hates.

5.2.10.s: yaḥ prathama ekāṣṭakāyāṃ jāyeta tam utsrakṣyann āgneyam aṣṭākapālaṃ nirupyotsṛjyāthāgnaye vaiśvānarāya dvādaśakapālaṃ māsimāsi nirvapet sam̐vatsaram /
5.2.10.d: यः प्रथम एकाष्टकायां जायेत तम् उत्स्रक्ष्यन्न् आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालं निरुप्योत्सृज्याथाग्नये वैश्वानराय द्वादशकपालं मासिमासि निर्वपेत् सम्̐वत्सरम् /
5.2.10.m: He who is born first on the Ekāṣṭakā day—intending to release him, having apportioned an eight-potsherd [cake] for Agni and released [the bull], he should then apportion a twelve-potsherd [cake] for Agni Vaiśvānara month by month for a year.

5.2.10.s: atha yo 'parasyām ekāṣṭakāyāṃ jāyeta tam evam evotsṛjet /
5.2.10.d: अथ यो ऽपरस्याम् एकाष्टकायां जायेत तम् एवम् एवोत्सृजेत् /
5.2.10.m: Then, he who is born on the second Ekāṣṭakā day, he should release in the very same way.

5.2.10.s: yadā pūrvotsṛṣṭo medhaṃ gached athendrāyābhimātighna ālabhetāśvo 'vyuptavaho dakṣiṇā /
5.2.10.d: यदा पूर्वोत्सृष्टो मेधं गछेद् अथेन्द्रायाभिमातिघ्न आलभेताश्वो ऽव्युप्तवहो दक्षिणा /
5.2.10.m: When the one released first attains fitness for sacrifice, then he should seize [him] for Indra, the slayer of adversaries; a horse with an unbroken neck is the sacrificial gift.

5.2.10.s: tad yadā dvitīyotsṛṣṭo medhaṃ gached athendrāya vṛtratura ālabheta / śatam avyuptavahā dakṣiṇā /
5.2.10.d: तद् यदा द्वितीयोत्सृष्टो मेधं गछेद् अथेन्द्राय वृत्रतुर आलभेत / शतम् अव्युप्तवहा दक्षिणा /
5.2.10.m: Then when the one released second attains fitness for sacrifice, then he should seize [him] for Indra, the overcome of Vṛtra; a hundred [draught animals] with unbroken necks are the sacrificial gift.

5.2.10.s: etābhyām iṣṭvā pāpmānaṃ bhrātṛvyam apahatya citrāyāḥ putram aruṇaṃ tūparaṃ brāhmaṇaspatyam ālabhetābhicaran /
5.2.10.d: एताभ्याम् इष्ट्वा पाप्मानं भ्रातृव्यम् अपहत्य चित्रायाः पुत्रम् अरुणं तूपरं ब्राह्मणस्पत्यम् आलभेताभिचरन् /
5.2.10.m: Having sacrificed with these two, having struck away evil, his rival, he should, when performing sorcery, seize a reddish hornless [bull], the son of a spotted cow, for Bṛhaspati.

5.2.10.s: yaḥ pāpmanā tamasā gṛhīto manyeta sa etam āśvinam añjim ālabheta /
5.2.10.d: यः पाप्मना तमसा गृहीतो मन्येत स एतम् आश्विनम् अञ्जिम् आलभेत /
5.2.10.m: He who considers himself seized by evil [and] darkness should seize this painted [victim] for the Aśvins.

5.2.10.s: tejaskāmo vasante lalāmam̐s trīn ṛṣabhān ālabheta / prāvṛṣi śitikakudaḥ śaradi śvetānūkāśāḥ / prājāpatyaṃ daśamaṃ dvādaśe māse //
5.2.10.d: तेजस्कामो वसन्ते ललामम्̐स् त्रीन् ऋषभान् आलभेत / प्रावृषि शितिककुदः शरदि श्वेतानूकाशाः / प्राजापत्यं दशमं द्वादशे मासे //
5.2.10.m: One who desires fiery splendour should seize three bulls with white forehead marks in spring; white-humped ones in the rainy season; white-backed ones in autumn; a tenth one for Prajāpati in the twelfth month.

5.2.10.s: namo mahimne \\ itiprabhṛtibhiḥ prāk sviṣṭakṛtaḥ sarveṣu pañcāhutīr juhoti /
5.2.10.d: नमो महिम्ने \\ इतिप्रभृतिभिः प्राक् स्विष्टकृतः सर्वेषु पञ्चाहुतीर् जुहोति /
5.2.10.m: Prior to the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he offers five libations in all of them with the [verses] beginning with: 'Homage to greatness.'

5.2.10.s: nānātantrāḥ kṛṣṇagrīvāḥ samānatantrā vā /
5.2.10.d: नानातन्त्राः कृष्णग्रीवाः समानतन्त्रा वा /
5.2.10.m: The black-necked ones have separate ritual frameworks, or they share a common ritual framework.

5.2.11.s: kaukilyāḥ sautrāmaṇyāḥ sa kalpo ya aiṣṭikyāḥ /
5.2.11.d: कौकिल्याः सौत्रामण्याः स कल्पो य ऐष्टिक्याः /
5.2.11.m: The ritual procedure of the Kaukilī Sautrāmaṇī is that of the sacrifice of cake and boiled oblation.
Those are desires, and [it is] for one who has vomited soma.

5.2.11.s: parīto ṣiñcatā sutam iti pratiduhā pariṣiñcaty ekasyā dugdhena prathamāyām̐ vyuṣṭāyāṃ dvayor dvitīyasyām /
5.2.11.d: परीतो षिञ्चता सुतम् इति प्रतिदुहा परिषिञ्चत्य् एकस्या दुग्धेन प्रथमायाम्̐ व्युष्टायां द्वयोर् द्वितीयस्याम् /
5.2.11.m: With 'Pour out the pressed [soma] all around', he pours [the liquor] all around with fresh milk: with the milk of one [cow] on the first dawn, of two on the second.
Saying 'The liquor is produced in three days', he fasts for the animal sacrifice.
On the next day, there is a bull for Indra; its first anuvāka contains the āprī-verses.
[The hymn] 'Approaching the active ones' consists of six verses.

5.2.11.s: śvobhūta udaṅṅ avasṛpya tripaśus tasmin surā /
5.2.11.d: श्वोभूत उदङ्ङ् अवसृप्य त्रिपशुस् तस्मिन् सुरा /
5.2.11.m: On the next day, having crept towards the north, there is the rite of three animals; in it is the liquor.

5.2.11.s: vāyuḥ pūtas \\ iti tām̐ somavāminaḥ kuryād vāyoḥ pūtas \\ iti tām̐ somātipavitasya //
5.2.11.d: वायुः पूतस् \\ इति ताम्̐ सोमवामिनः कुर्याद् वायोः पूतस् \\ इति ताम्̐ सोमातिपवितस्य //
5.2.11.m: He should perform that [formula] 'Purified by Vāyu' for one who has vomited soma, [and] 'Purified from Vāyu' for one excessively purged by soma.
He recites after: 'The spiritual power, the temporal power...'

5.2.11.s: kuvid aṅga yavamantas \\ iti gṛhṇīto 'dhvaryuḥ payograhān /
5.2.11.d: कुविद् अङ्ग यवमन्तस् \\ इति गृह्णीतो ऽध्वर्युः पयोग्रहान् /
5.2.11.m: With 'Truly, indeed, those who have barley...', the adhvaryu draws the cups of milk.

5.2.11.s: kuvalasaktubhir godhūmasaktubhir vṛkalomnāśvinam̐ śrītvā sādayati karkandhusaktubhir upavākāsaktubhir vyāghralomnā sārasvataṃ badarasaktubhis tokmasaktubhiḥ sim̐halomnaindram /
5.2.11.d: कुवलसक्तुभिर् गोधूमसक्तुभिर् वृकलोम्नाश्विनम्̐ श्रीत्वा सादयति कर्कन्धुसक्तुभिर् उपवाकासक्तुभिर् व्याघ्रलोम्ना सारस्वतं बदरसक्तुभिस् तोक्मसक्तुभिः सिम्̐हलोम्नैन्द्रम् /
5.2.11.m: Having mixed [the cup] for the Aśvins with jujube-groats, wheat-groats, and wolf-hair, he deposits it; the one for Sarasvatī with berry-groats, upavāka-groats, and tiger-hair; the one for Indra with common jujube-groats, malted-grain-groats, and lion-hair.
From the hole for the sacrificial post onward, [the procedure is] established up to the dedication [of the animals].

5.2.11.s: aśvibhyām̐ sarasvatyā indrāyājam̐ sarasvatyā indrāyāśvibhyāṃ meṣīm indrāyāśvibhyām̐ sarasvatyā ṛṣabham /
5.2.11.d: अश्विभ्याम्̐ सरस्वत्या इन्द्रायाजम्̐ सरस्वत्या इन्द्रायाश्विभ्यां मेषीम् इन्द्रायाश्विभ्याम्̐ सरस्वत्या ऋषभम् /
5.2.11.m: [He dedicates] a goat to the Aśvins, to Sarasvatī, and to Indra; a ewe to Sarasvatī, to Indra, and to the Aśvins; a bull to Indra, to the Aśvins, and to Sarasvatī.

5.2.11.s: yā vyāghram̐ viṣūcikā \\ iti śyenapattreṇa yajamānaṃ pāvayati /
5.2.11.d: या व्याघ्रम्̐ विषूचिका \\ इति श्येनपत्त्रेण यजमानं पावयति /
5.2.11.m: With 'The cholera which [attacks] the tiger...', he purifies the sacrificer with a falcon feather.

5.2.11.s: pāvitaḥ somo rājā \\ ity anuvākena grahān upatiṣṭhate //
5.2.11.d: पावितः सोमो राजा \\ इत्य् अनुवाकेन ग्रहान् उपतिष्ठते //
5.2.11.m: With the anuvāka beginning with 'Purified is King Soma...', he reveres the cups.
Having responded with "surāvantam...", they offer when the vaṣaṭ and the second vaṣaṭ have been made.

5.2.11.s: dhyānāni dhyātvā yam aśvinā \\ iti payograhān bhakṣayati // nānā hi vām iti surāgrahān /
5.2.11.d: ध्यानानि ध्यात्वा यम् अश्विना \\ इति पयोग्रहान् भक्षयति // नाना हि वाम् इति सुराग्रहान् /
5.2.11.m: Having meditated on the meditations, he consumes the milk-cups with "yam aśvinā...", and the surā-cups with "nānā hi vām...".

5.2.11.s: pratiduho vājaprasavyam̐ hutvottarata uttaraveder āsandyām āsīnaṃ devasya tvā savituḥ prasave \\ iti saṃpātenābhiṣiñcati śiraso 'dhy ā mukhād avasrāvayati / śeṣaṃ pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇasmin bhūḥ svāhā \\ iti juhoti //
5.2.11.d: प्रतिदुहो वाजप्रसव्यम्̐ हुत्वोत्तरत उत्तरवेदेर् आसन्द्याम् आसीनं देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे \\ इति संपातेनाभिषिञ्चति शिरसो ऽध्य् आ मुखाद् अवस्रावयति / शेषं प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणस्मिन् भूः स्वाहा \\ इति जुहोति //
5.2.11.m: Having offered the fresh milk counter-clockwise, he sprinkles [the sacrificer], who is seated on a stool to the north of the uttaravedi, with the residue [of the offering] using "devasya tvā savituḥ prasave...", and causes it to flow down over the head down to the mouth. The pratiprasthātṛ priest offers the remainder in the southern [fire] with "bhūḥ svāhā".

5.2.11.s: śiro me śrīr yaśo mukham iti yathāliṅgam aṅgāni saṃmṛśati //
5.2.11.d: शिरो मे श्रीर् यशो मुखम् इति यथालिङ्गम् अङ्गानि संमृशति //
5.2.11.m: With "śiro me śrīr yaśo mukham...", he touches his limbs according to the characteristic marks [in the sacred formula].
With "prati brahmann...", he steps down [from the stool].

5.2.11.s: yūṣṇaḥ śṛṅgaśaphaiḥ sīsena tantram itiprabhṛtibhiḥ prāk sviṣṭakṛtaḥ ṣoḍaśāhutīr juhoti /
5.2.11.d: यूष्णः शृङ्गशफैः सीसेन तन्त्रम् इतिप्रभृतिभिः प्राक् स्विष्टकृतः षोडशाहुतीर् जुहोति /
5.2.11.m: Before the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he offers sixteen oblations with [the sacred formulas] beginning with "yūṣṇaḥ śṛṅgaśaphaiḥ sīsena tantram...".
He causes [water] to trickle through the hundred-holed strainer.

5.2.11.s: punantu mā pitaras \\ iti yajamānam̐ vācayati //
5.2.11.d: पुनन्तु मा पितरस् \\ इति यजमानम्̐ वाचयति //
5.2.11.m: He makes the sacrificer recite "punantu mā pitaras...".

5.2.11.s: ye samānāḥ samanasas \\ ity adhvaryur juhoti // ye samānāḥ samanasas \\ jīvā jīveṣu māmakās \\ iti pratiprasthātā //
5.2.11.d: ये समानाः समनसस् \\ इत्य् अध्वर्युर् जुहोति // ये समानाः समनसस् \\ जीवा जीवेषु मामकास् \\ इति प्रतिप्रस्थाता //
5.2.11.m: The adhvaryu priest offers with "ye samānāḥ samanasas..."; the pratiprasthātṛ priest with "ye samānāḥ samanaso jīvā jīveṣu māmakāḥ...".

5.2.11.s: dve srutī ity adhvaryur idam̐ havir iti pratiprasthātā /
5.2.11.d: द्वे स्रुती इत्य् अध्वर्युर् इदम्̐ हविर् इति प्रतिप्रस्थाता /
5.2.11.m: The adhvaryu priest [offers] with "dve srutī..."; the pratiprasthātṛ priest with "idam havir...".

5.2.11.s: ekādaśakapālān paśupuroḍāśān nirvapatīndrāya sutrāmṇe savitre varuṇāya savitre varuṇāyendrāya sutrāmṇe varuṇāyendrāya sutrāmṇe savitre /
5.2.11.d: एकादशकपालान् पशुपुरोडाशान् निर्वपतीन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे सवित्रे वरुणाय सवित्रे वरुणायेन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे वरुणायेन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे सवित्रे /
5.2.11.m: He apportions animal-cakes on eleven potsherds: to Indra Sutrāman, to Savitṛ, to Varuṇa; [or] to Savitṛ, to Varuṇa, to Indra Sutrāman; [or] to Varuṇa, to Indra Sutrāman, to Savitṛ.
[The ritual is] established up to the time of the sacrificial gifts.

5.2.11.s: trayastrim̐śad dakṣiṇās tāsāṃ dhenur vaḍabā cānukiśorā //
5.2.11.d: त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शद् दक्षिणास् तासां धेनुर् वडबा चानुकिशोरा //
5.2.11.m: The sacrificial gifts are thirty-three; among them are a milch cow and a mare with a foal.

5.2.11.s: yad devā devaheḍanam itiprabhṛtibhiḥ prāk samiṣṭayajurbhyas tisra āhutīr juhoti //
5.2.11.d: यद् देवा देवहेडनम् इतिप्रभृतिभिः प्राक् समिष्टयजुर्भ्यस् तिस्र आहुतीर् जुहोति //
5.2.11.m: Before the samiṣṭayajus formulas, he offers three oblations with [the sacred formulas] beginning with "yad devā devaheḍanam...".

5.2.11.s: dhāmnodhāmnas \\ ity avabhṛthe 'psu juhoti // yad grāme yad araṇye \\ iti dvitīyām //
5.2.11.d: धाम्नोधाम्नस् \\ इत्य् अवभृथे ऽप्सु जुहोति // यद् ग्रामे यद् अरण्ये \\ इति द्वितीयाम् //
5.2.11.m: At the purificatory bath, he offers into the water with "dhāmnodhāmnaḥ..."; the second with "yad grāme yad araṇye...".

5.2.11.s: pavitram asi \\ iti snātāv anyonyasya pṛṣṭhaṃ prakṣālayataḥ //
5.2.11.d: पवित्रम् असि \\ इति स्नाताव् अन्योन्यस्य पृष्ठं प्रक्षालयतः //
5.2.11.m: With "pavitram asi...", having bathed, the two wash each other's back.

5.2.11.s: samāvṛtat pṛthivī \\ iti sruveṇa gārhapatye juhoti /
5.2.11.d: समावृतत् पृथिवी \\ इति स्रुवेण गार्हपत्ये जुहोति /
5.2.11.m: With "samāvṛtat pṛthivī...", he offers into the gārhapatya fire with the dipping spoon.
The second and third are the calls for the āprī verses. At the fourth are the portions of omentum.

5.2.11.s: paśupuroḍāśahaviḥsv iṣṭakṛtām̐ yājyānuvākyā yā yājyās tāḥ puronuvākyā yāḥ puronuvākyās tā yājyā vapāpaśupuroḍāśahaviṣām /
5.2.11.d: पशुपुरोडाशहविःस्व् इष्टकृताम्̐ याज्यानुवाक्या या याज्यास् ताः पुरोनुवाक्या याः पुरोनुवाक्यास् ता याज्या वपापशुपुरोडाशहविषाम् /
5.2.11.m: For the Sviṣṭakṛt offerings of the animal-cakes and oblations, the offering verses are the invitatory verses, and the invitatory verses are the offering verses of the omentum, animal-cakes, and oblations.
On the next day, there is a bull for Indra Vayodhas; his penultimate [verse] is the āprī verse.
The final six verses are the invitatory and offering verses.
The penultimate [verse] is for the sarvapṛṣṭhā [oblation].
The final [verse] is for the horse sacrifice; the ritual framework is that of the mṛgāreṣṭi.

5.2.12.s: prāg vedikālād ekādaśa yūpān achaity upaśayaṃ pātnīvataṃ ca /
5.2.12.d: प्राग् वेदिकालाद् एकादश यूपान् अछैत्य् उपशयं पात्नीवतं च /
5.2.12.m: Prior to the time of the altar, he cuts eleven sacrificial posts, as well as the upaśaya post and the one for the wife's sacrifice.
Beginning with the selection, each [is handled] individually in sequence.

5.2.12.s: prathamotpatitam̐ svarucaṣālam agniṣṭham abhito yūpān asthūlān anaṇūn tulyān samūlān /
5.2.12.d: प्रथमोत्पतितम्̐ स्वरुचषालम् अग्निष्ठम् अभितो यूपान् अस्थूलान् अनणून् तुल्यान् समूलान् /
5.2.12.m: The first that has fallen, having its own post-ring, is the central post; around it are posts that are not too thick, not too thin, equal, and possessing roots.

5.2.12.s: ekādaśa yūpān parimāya traidham̐ saṃbhujya tṛtīyaiḥ pramāya vedim̐ vidadhāti /
5.2.12.d: एकादश यूपान् परिमाय त्रैधम्̐ संभुज्य तृतीयैः प्रमाय वेदिम्̐ विदधाति /
5.2.12.m: Having measured the eleven sacrificial posts, dividing [the length] into three and measuring by the thirds, he lays out the altar.

5.2.12.s: agniṣṭhe dve raśane parivīya tūṣṇīm̐ vim̐śatiṃ parivyayati /
5.2.12.d: अग्निष्ठे द्वे रशने परिवीय तूष्णीम्̐ विम्̐शतिं परिव्ययति /
5.2.12.m: Having wound two cords around the central post, he winds twenty around silently.

5.2.12.s: śvobhūta āśvinaṃ gṛhītvāgniṣṭhād udañcam̐ rathākṣaṃ pramāya sphyena yūpāvaṭaṃ parilikhati vyatyāsam itarān /
5.2.12.d: श्वोभूत आश्विनं गृहीत्वाग्निष्ठाद् उदञ्चम्̐ रथाक्षं प्रमाय स्फ्येन यूपावटं परिलिखति व्यत्यासम् इतरान् /
5.2.12.m: On the next day, having drawn the cup for the Aśvins, measuring a chariot axle northwards from the central post, he outlines the post-hole with the wooden sword, and alternately for the others.
Beginning with the anointing, each [action] is established for each individual post up to the wrapping [with the cord].

5.2.12.s: dakṣiṇasmin yūpāntare prāñcam upaśayaṃ nidhāya yūpā āñjanīyās tūṣṇīm̐ svaruraśanam /
5.2.12.d: दक्षिणस्मिन् यूपान्तरे प्राञ्चम् उपशयं निधाय यूपा आञ्जनीयास् तूष्णीम्̐ स्वरुरशनम् /
5.2.12.m: Having placed the upaśaya post pointing east in the southern interval between the posts, the posts are to be anointed, and the post-chip and cord [are attached] silently.

5.2.12.s: yady abhicared idam aham amum āmuṣyāyaṇam amuṣyāḥ putram indravajreṇābhinidadhāmi \\ ity abhinidadhyāt /
5.2.12.d: यद्य् अभिचरेद् इदम् अहम् अमुम् आमुष्यायणम् अमुष्याः पुत्रम् इन्द्रवज्रेणाभिनिदधामि \\ इत्य् अभिनिदध्यात् /
5.2.12.m: If he performs sorcery, he should set it down with: "Here I set down so-and-so, descendant of so-and-so, son of such-and-such a woman, with Indra's thunderbolt."

5.2.12.s: udakpravaṇa ekādaśinīm̐ saṃminoti trīn vā madhyataḥ samān /
5.2.12.d: उदक्प्रवण एकादशिनीम्̐ संमिनोति त्रीन् वा मध्यतः समान् /
5.2.12.m: He erects the set of eleven posts sloping towards the north, or three equal ones in the middle.

5.2.12.s: sam̐srāviṇī vṛṣṭikāmasyāgniṣṭho hrasiṣṭho 'nupūrvam itare varṣīyām̐sa ārāgrābhicarato 'gniṣṭho varṣiṣṭho 'nupūrvam itare hrasīyām̐saḥ samāḥ pratiṣṭhākāmasya /
5.2.12.d: सम्̐स्राविणी वृष्टिकामस्याग्निष्ठो ह्रसिष्ठो ऽनुपूर्वम् इतरे वर्षीयाम्̐स आराग्राभिचरतो ऽग्निष्ठो वर्षिष्ठो ऽनुपूर्वम् इतरे ह्रसीयाम्̐सः समाः प्रतिष्ठाकामस्य /
5.2.12.m: For one desirous of rain, [they are] flowing together: the central post is shortest, and the others successively taller; for one practicing sorcery, [they are shaped like] the point of an awl: the central post is tallest, and the others successively shorter; for one desirous of a firm standing, they are equal.
Or he may erect them on the preceding day.

5.2.12.s: agniṣṭhāt tu śvobhūte raśanāḥ parivīya paśūn upākaroti /
5.2.12.d: अग्निष्ठात् तु श्वोभूते रशनाः परिवीय पशून् उपाकरोति /
5.2.12.m: On the next day, however, having wound the cords starting from the central post, he brings forward the sacrificial animals.

5.2.12.s: kṛṣṇaśirasam ajam āgneyam agniṣṭhe niyunakti sārasvatīṃ meṣīm uttarasmin saumyaṃ babhruṃ dakṣiṇasmin vyatyāsam itarān vāruṇaṃ dakṣiṇārdhe /
5.2.12.d: कृष्णशिरसम् अजम् आग्नेयम् अग्निष्ठे नियुनक्ति सारस्वतीं मेषीम् उत्तरस्मिन् सौम्यं बभ्रुं दक्षिणस्मिन् व्यत्यासम् इतरान् वारुणं दक्षिणार्धे /
5.2.12.m: He binds a black-headed he-goat sacred to Agni to the central post; a ewe sacred to Sarasvatī to the northern one; a brown one sacred to Soma to the southern one; the others alternately; and the one sacred to Varuṇa in the southern half.
For the upaśaya post, he should designate a wild animal.

5.2.12.s: abhicarann asau te paśur iti dveṣyaṃ nirdiśet /
5.2.12.d: अभिचरन्न् असौ ते पशुर् इति द्वेष्यं निर्दिशेत् /
5.2.12.m: If practicing sorcery, he should designate the hated person with: "That one is your animal."

5.2.12.s: agreṇa yūpāvaṭam apareṇottarān paśūn mukhyaprathamāñ śāmitrāya nayanti /
5.2.12.d: अग्रेण यूपावटम् अपरेणोत्तरान् पशून् मुख्यप्रथमाञ् शामित्राय नयन्ति /
5.2.12.m: In front of the post-hole and to the west of the northern ones, they lead the animals to the slaughtering place, beginning with the principal one.
They place them each to the north, or each to the east.

5.2.12.s: sarveṣūpāsanāḥ saha raśanā anuprāsyanti darbhān vapāśrapaṇīḥ svarūm̐ś ca /
5.2.12.d: सर्वेषूपासनाः सह रशना अनुप्रास्यन्ति दर्भान् वपाश्रपणीः स्वरूम्̐श् च /
5.2.12.m: At all [posts], they throw in the attendants together with the cords, sacrificial grass, omentum-spits, and post-chips.
[The ritual is] established up to the extraction of the omentum.

5.2.12.s: apareṇottarān paśūn mukhyaprathamāḥ śāmitrād dharanti samayā paśuṃpaśuṃ parigrāhaṃ pūrvāṅgārān āhavanīyāya //
5.2.12.d: अपरेणोत्तरान् पशून् मुख्यप्रथमाः शामित्राद् धरन्ति समया पशुंपशुं परिग्राहं पूर्वाङ्गारान् आहवनीयाय //
5.2.12.m: To the west of the northern animals, beginning with the principal one, they carry the enclosure around animal by animal from the slaughtering place, and the eastern coals for the āhavanīya fire.

5.2.12.s: svāhā devebhyas \\ iti purastād vapānāṃ juhuyād viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā \\ ity upariṣṭāt /
5.2.12.d: स्वाहा देवेभ्यस् \\ इति पुरस्ताद् वपानां जुहुयाद् विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यः स्वाहा \\ इत्य् उपरिष्टात् /
5.2.12.m: He should offer before the omenta with "svāhā devebhyaḥ...", and after them with "viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā...".
Except for the soma-day victims, there are heart-spits and animal-cakes.
When they have the same deity and are uninterrupted, there is a single recitation of the manotā verse; when interrupted, [one] for each animal.

5.2.12.s: śeṣair antar anto diśaḥ pratījyādhyūdhnīm̐ hotre haranti vaniṣṭhum agnīdhe /
5.2.12.d: शेषैर् अन्तर् अन्तो दिशः प्रतीज्याध्यूध्नीम्̐ होत्रे हरन्ति वनिष्ठुम् अग्नीधे /
5.2.12.m: Having offered with the remainders towards the various directions within the boundaries, they carry the portion above the udder to the hotṛ priest, and the entrails to the āgnīdhra priest.
Having cut off together [portions] of the entrails, he makes an additional offering.
They cause the wives to offer the wife-offerings with the tail-portions.
Before the anūbandhyā cow, they proceed in the east-roofed hall with the victim for the wife's sacrifice.
The vedi is according to the New-Moon sacrifice; the clarified butters are according to the animal sacrifice.

5.2.12.s: agreṇa gārhapatyam adhonābhim acaṣālam̐ yūpaṃ saṃminoti /
5.2.12.d: अग्रेण गार्हपत्यम् अधोनाभिम् अचषालम्̐ यूपं संमिनोति /
5.2.12.m: East of the gārhapatya, below the navel [in height], without a top-ring, he erects the sacrificial post.
The post-hole is not strewn [with grass].
He assigns the animal sacred to Tvaṣṭṛ.
Having released it, fire having been carried around it together with the halter, he concludes [the rite] with clarified butter.

5.2.12.s: yāvanti paśor avadānāni tāvat kṛtva ājyasyāvadāya tvaṣṭra ājyasyānubrūhi \\ iti tvaṣṭra ājyasya preṣya \\ iti pracarati /
5.2.12.d: यावन्ति पशोर् अवदानानि तावत् कृत्व आज्यस्यावदाय त्वष्ट्र आज्यस्यानुब्रूहि \\ इति त्वष्ट्र आज्यस्य प्रेष्य \\ इति प्रचरति /
5.2.12.m: Having cut off as many portions of clarified butter as there are portions of the animal, he proceeds with: 'Recite [the invitatory verse] for Tvaṣṭṛ of the clarified butter', and 'Prompt [the offering verse] for Tvaṣṭṛ of the clarified butter'.

5.2.12.s: vapāsthāne paśupuroḍāśasya paśor ājyena sviṣṭakṛd ājyenopayajaḥ /
5.2.12.d: वपास्थाने पशुपुरोडाशस्य पशोर् आज्येन स्विष्टकृद् आज्येनोपयजः /
5.2.12.m: In place of the omentum [is the offering] of the animal cake; the Sviṣṭakṛt offering of the animal is made with clarified butter; the auxiliary offering is made with clarified butter.
It concludes with the śaṃyu [formula].
He takes hold of all the ladles together.
Having concluded the anūbandhyā cow, he assigns the sacrificial posts.

5.2.12.s: kratupaśubhir ekādaśinī nirvarteta / niyatā sāgnicityeṣv ekādaśiny ekayūpe yūpaikādaśinī sarvastomeṣu /
5.2.12.d: क्रतुपशुभिर् एकादशिनी निर्वर्तेत / नियता साग्निचित्येष्व् एकादशिन्य् एकयूपे यूपैकादशिनी सर्वस्तोमेषु /
5.2.12.m: A set of eleven [animals] should be performed with the sacrificial animals of the rite. The set of eleven [animals] is fixed in the rites with the piling of the fire altar; in a single sacrificial post, [or] a set of eleven sacrificial posts in all-stoma sacrifices.

5.2.13.s: yajamānayajñapativādān ūhet samavāye // anu vām \ anu vaḥ / \ anumantau \ anumantaḥ / \ āvahataṃ \ āvahata / \ devāyadbhyāṃ \ devāyadbhyaḥ / \ ye badhyāmānau \ ye badhyamānān / \ svarvidau sthaḥ \ svarvidaḥ stha / \ svar itam \\ svar ita / \ lokavidau sthas \\ lokavidaḥ stha / \ lokam itam \\ lokamita / \ nāthavidau sthas \\ nāthavidaḥ stha / \ nātham itam \\ nātham ita / \ gātuvidau sthas \\ gātuvidaḥ stha / \ gātum itam \\ gātum ita / \ mriyethe \ mriyadhve / \ riṣyathaḥ \ riṣyatha / \ idithaḥ \ iditha / \ pāśābhyāṃ paśū \ pāśebhyaḥ paśūn / \ mārutaṃ devaṃ gachatam \\ mārutaṃ devaṃ gachata / \ śamitārā3u \ śamitāraḥ / \ tatra vām \\ tatra vaḥ / \ bhūri vām \\ bhūri vaḥ / \ divam̐ vām \\ divam̐ vaḥ / \ yantau \ yataḥ /
5.2.13.d: यजमानयज्ञपतिवादान् ऊहेत् समवाये // अनु वाम् \ अनु वः / \ अनुमन्तौ \ अनुमन्तः / \ आवहतं \ आवहत / \ देवायद्भ्यां \ देवायद्भ्यः / \ ये बध्यामानौ \ ये बध्यमानान् / \ स्वर्विदौ स्थः \ स्वर्विदः स्थ / \ स्वर् इतम् \\ स्वर् इत / \ लोकविदौ स्थस् \\ लोकविदः स्थ / \ लोकम् इतम् \\ लोकमित / \ नाथविदौ स्थस् \\ नाथविदः स्थ / \ नाथम् इतम् \\ नाथम् इत / \ गातुविदौ स्थस् \\ गातुविदः स्थ / \ गातुम् इतम् \\ गातुम् इत / \ म्रियेथे \ म्रियध्वे / \ रिष्यथः \ रिष्यथ / \ इदिथः \ इदिथ / \ पाशाभ्यां पशू \ पाशेभ्यः पशून् / \ मारुतं देवं गछतम् \\ मारुतं देवं गछत / \ शमितारा3उ \ शमितारः / \ तत्र वाम् \\ तत्र वः / \ भूरि वाम् \\ भूरि वः / \ दिवम्̐ वाम् \\ दिवम्̐ वः / \ यन्तौ \ यतः /
5.2.13.m: In case of combination [of two or more animals], he should adapt the expressions concerning the sacrificer and the lord of sacrifice: 'after you two' / 'after you [all]'; 'two assenters' / 'assenters'; 'bring you two' / 'bring you [all]'; 'for the two seeking the gods' / 'for those seeking the gods'; 'who [are] being bound' [dual] / 'who [are] being bound' [plural]; 'you two are finders of heaven' / 'you [all] are finders of heaven'; 'go to heaven' [dual] / 'go to heaven' [plural]; 'you two are finders of the world' / 'you [all] are finders of the world'; 'go to the world' [dual] / 'go to the world' [plural]; 'you two are finders of a protector' / 'you [all] are finders of a protector'; 'go to a protector' [dual] / 'go to a protector' [plural]; 'you two are finders of the path' / 'you [all] are finders of the path'; 'go to the path' [dual] / 'go to the path' [plural]; 'you two die' / 'you [all] die'; 'you two are injured' / 'you [all] are injured'; 'you two go' / 'you [all] go'; 'the two animals from the two fetters' / 'the animals from the fetters'; 'go you two to the Marut god' / 'go you [all] to the Marut god'; 'O two slaughterers' / 'O slaughterers'; 'there for you two' / 'there for you [all]'; 'abundant for you two' / 'abundant for you [all]'; 'the sky for you two' / 'the sky for you [all]'; 'the two going' / 'those going'.
The remainder is not to be adapted; 'mother, father' has been explained.

5.2.14.s: cittiḥ srug iti daśahotā \\ indraṃ gacha svāhā \\ iti homaḥ //
5.2.14.d: चित्तिः स्रुग् इति दशहोता \\ इन्द्रं गछ स्वाहा \\ इति होमः //
5.2.14.m: 'Thought is the ladle' is the Daśahotṛ formula; the oblation is with: 'Go to Indra, svāhā'.

5.2.14.s: pṛthivī hotā \\ iti caturhotā // vācaspate vāco vīryeṇa \\ iti grahaḥ // somaḥ somasya pibatu \\ iti dvitīyaḥ /
5.2.14.d: पृथिवी होता \\ इति चतुर्होता // वाचस्पते वाचो वीर्येण \\ इति ग्रहः // सोमः सोमस्य पिबतु \\ इति द्वितीयः /
5.2.14.m: 'Earth is the hotṛ' is the Caturhotṛ formula. The drawing [formula] is: 'O lord of speech, by the power of speech'. The second is: 'Let Soma drink of Soma'.

5.2.14.s: agnir hotā \\ iti pañcahotā // vācaspate hinvidhe nāman \\ iti grahaḥ // somaḥ somasya pibatu \\ iti dvitīyaḥ //
5.2.14.d: अग्निर् होता \\ इति पञ्चहोता // वाचस्पते हिन्विधे नामन् \\ इति ग्रहः // सोमः सोमस्य पिबतु \\ इति द्वितीयः //
5.2.14.m: 'Agni is the hotṛ' is the Pañcahotṛ formula. The drawing [formula] is: 'O lord of speech, stimulate into the name of the rite'. The second is: 'Let Soma drink of Soma'.

5.2.14.s: mahāhavir hotā \\ iti saptahotā // vidhe nāman \\ iti grahaḥ /
5.2.14.d: महाहविर् होता \\ इति सप्तहोता // विधे नामन् \\ इति ग्रहः /
5.2.14.m: 'The great oblation is the hotṛ' is the Saptahotṛ formula. The drawing [formula] is: 'Into the name of the rite'.

5.2.14.s: apa upaspṛśya prāṅmukhaḥ pratigṛhṇāti deyam̐ vābhimukhaḥ /
5.2.14.d: अप उपस्पृश्य प्राङ्मुखः प्रतिगृह्णाति देयम्̐ वाभिमुखः /
5.2.14.m: Having touched water, facing east he accepts [the gift], or facing that which is to be given.

5.2.14.s: sāvitraḥ purastāt sarveṣām //
5.2.14.d: सावित्रः पुरस्तात् सर्वेषाम् //
5.2.14.m: [The formula] sacred to Savitṛ is placed before all [acceptances].

5.2.14.s: yamāya tvā \\ ity aśvam̐ yac caikaśapham //
5.2.14.d: यमाय त्वा \\ इत्य् अश्वम्̐ यच् चैकशफम् //
5.2.14.m: 'To Yama thee' for a horse and whatever has uncloven hooves.

5.2.14.s: rudrāya tvā \\ iti dviśapham //
5.2.14.d: रुद्राय त्वा \\ इति द्विशफम् //
5.2.14.m: 'To Rudra thee' for an animal with cloven hooves.

5.2.14.s: agnaye tvā \\ iti hiraṇyamṃ trapuḥ sīsamayo lohaṃ ca //
5.2.14.d: अग्नये त्वा \\ इति हिरण्यम्ं त्रपुः सीसमयो लोहं च //
5.2.14.m: 'To Agni thee' for gold, tin, lead, iron, and copper.

5.2.14.s: gnās tvākṛntan \\ apaso 'tanvata \ dhiyo 'vayan \ bṛhaspataye tvā \\ iti vāsaḥ //
5.2.14.d: ग्नास् त्वाकृन्तन् \\ अपसो ऽतन्वत \ धियो ऽवयन् \ बृहस्पतये त्वा \\ इति वासः //
5.2.14.m: 'The wives cut thee, the active women stretched [thee], the thoughtful women wove [thee], to Bṛhaspati thee' for a garment.

5.2.14.s: prajāpataye tvā \\ iti hastinaṃ puruṣam̐ vrīhiyavau bhūmiṃ prāṇi cānyat //
5.2.14.d: प्रजापतये त्वा \\ इति हस्तिनं पुरुषम्̐ व्रीहियवौ भूमिं प्राणि चान्यत् //
5.2.14.m: 'To Prajāpati thee' for an elephant, a human being, rice and barley, land, and other living beings.

5.2.14.s: uttānāya tvā \\ ity aprāṇi //
5.2.14.d: उत्तानाय त्वा \\ इत्य् अप्राणि //
5.2.14.m: 'To Uttāna thee' for what is inanimate.

5.2.14.s: ka idaṃ kasmā adād iti sarvatrānuṣajati kāmaitat te \\ ity antam /
5.2.14.d: क इदं कस्मा अदाद् इति सर्वत्रानुषजति कामैतत् ते \\ इत्य् अन्तम् /
5.2.14.m: He connects everywhere: 'Who gave this to whom?', ending with: 'O desire, this to thee'.

5.2.14.s: yaḥ prajayā paśubhir na prajāyeta drahilam ahatam̐ vāsaḥ paridhāya dvādaśarātraṃ taptaṃ payaḥ piban vratacāry adhaḥ śayīta /
5.2.14.d: यः प्रजया पशुभिर् न प्रजायेत द्रहिलम् अहतम्̐ वासः परिधाय द्वादशरात्रं तप्तं पयः पिबन् व्रतचार्य् अधः शयीत /
5.2.14.m: He who does not multiply in offspring and animals, having put on a strong, unwashed garment, drinking heated milk for twelve nights, observing a vow, should sleep on the ground.

5.2.14.s: trayodaśyām udite daśahotāraṃ nigadya \\ indraṃ gacha svāhā \\ iti homaḥ /
5.2.14.d: त्रयोदश्याम् उदिते दशहोतारं निगद्य \\ इन्द्रं गछ स्वाहा \\ इति होमः /
5.2.14.m: At sunrise on the thirteenth day, having pronounced the Daśahotṛ formula, the oblation is with: 'Go to Indra, svāhā'.

5.2.14.s: prāṇya \\ indraṃ gacha svāhā \\ ity apāne /
5.2.14.d: प्राण्य \\ इन्द्रं गछ स्वाहा \\ इत्य् अपाने /
5.2.14.m: Having inhaled, [he offers] on the out-breath with: 'Go to Indra, svāhā'.

5.2.14.s: caturhotāraṃ nigaded vyākhyātaḥ /
5.2.14.d: चतुर्होतारं निगदेद् व्याख्यातः /
5.2.14.m: He should pronounce the Caturhotṛ formula; it has been explained.

5.2.14.s: tathā pañcahotrā ṣaḍḍhotrā yaśaskāmaḥ /
5.2.14.d: तथा पञ्चहोत्रा षड्ढोत्रा यशस्कामः /
5.2.14.m: Likewise, one desiring glory [should act] with the Pañcahotṛ and the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formulas.

5.2.14.s: ṛtumukheṣu sam̐vatsaraṃ juhuyāt /
5.2.14.d: ऋतुमुखेषु सम्̐वत्सरं जुहुयात् /
5.2.14.m: He should offer at the beginnings of the seasons for a year.

5.2.14.s: someneṣṭvā pāpīyān manyamānaḥ saptahotāraṃ manasānudrutya vidhe nāman \\ iti graheṇa juhoti /
5.2.14.d: सोमेनेष्ट्वा पापीयान् मन्यमानः सप्तहोतारं मनसानुद्रुत्य विधे नामन् \\ इति ग्रहेण जुहोति /
5.2.14.m: Having sacrificed with Soma, one who considers himself worse off, having mentally recited the Saptahotṛ formula, offers with the drawing [formula]: 'Into the name of the rite'.

5.2.14.s: teṣām̐ vratāni / tribhiḥ sahaikataḥ sam̐vatsaraṃ nāśnīyāt trayāṇām ucchiṣṭaṃ na bhuñjīta / tribhyo na prayachet /
5.2.14.d: तेषाम्̐ व्रतानि / त्रिभिः सहैकतः सम्̐वत्सरं नाश्नीयात् त्रयाणाम् उच्छिष्टं न भुञ्जीत / त्रिभ्यो न प्रयछेत् /
5.2.14.m: Their vows: he should not eat together with three persons for a year; he should not eat the leftovers of three; he should not give to three.

5.2.14.s: yo 'dhītaḥ san na virodheta so 'raṇyaṃ paretya brāhmaṇaṃ bahuvidam upaveśya darbhastambam udgrathya caturhotṝn svakarmaṇo vyācakṣīta /
5.2.14.d: यो ऽधीतः सन् न विरोधेत सो ऽरण्यं परेत्य ब्राह्मणं बहुविदम् उपवेश्य दर्भस्तम्बम् उद्ग्रथ्य चतुर्होतॄन् स्वकर्मणो व्याचक्षीत /
5.2.14.m: He who, having studied, does not prosper, having gone to the wilderness and seated a learned brahmin, having tied a clump of darbha grass, should explain the Caturhotṛ formulas according to his own ritual.

5.2.14.s: nadīparvatamaryādāvyavahitāḥ sutyāḥ samānakālāḥ samṛtayajñāḥ /
5.2.14.d: नदीपर्वतमर्यादाव्यवहिताः सुत्याः समानकालाः समृतयज्ञाः /
5.2.14.m: Soma-pressing days separated by boundaries of rivers or mountains, occurring at the same time, are conflicting sacrifices.

5.2.14.s: tasya purastāt prātaranuvākasya samiddhe 'gnau saṃbhārayajūm̐ṣi juhoti yathā dīkṣaṇīyāyāḥ /
5.2.14.d: तस्य पुरस्तात् प्रातरनुवाकस्य समिद्धे ऽग्नौ संभारयजूम्̐षि जुहोति यथा दीक्षणीयायाः /
5.2.14.m: Before the morning recitation, on the kindled fire, he offers the saṃbhāra-yajus formulas, as in the case of the initiatory offering.

5.2.14.s: etair dvādaśāhe purastāt prāyaṇīyasya juhuyāt /
5.2.14.d: एतैर् द्वादशाहे पुरस्तात् प्रायणीयस्य जुहुयात् /
5.2.14.m: With these he should offer before the introductory rite at the twelve-day sacrifice.

5.2.14.s: etair evātithyam abhimṛśet /
5.2.14.d: एतैर् एवातिथ्यम् अभिमृशेत् /
5.2.14.m: With these very [formulas] he should touch the hospitality offering.

5.2.14.s: etāny evāgnīdhe 'nubrūyāt /
5.2.14.d: एतान्य् एवाग्नीधे ऽनुब्रूयात् /
5.2.14.m: These very [formulas] he should recite to the āgnīdhra.

5.2.14.s: etair antarā tvaṣṭāraṃ ca patnīś ca sam̐vatsaraṃ prajākāmo juhuyāt /
5.2.14.d: एतैर् अन्तरा त्वष्टारं च पत्नीश् च सम्̐वत्सरं प्रजाकामो जुहुयात् /
5.2.14.m: One desiring offspring should offer with these between Tvaṣṭṛ and the wives for a year.

5.2.15.s: bhūpate bhuvanapate mahato bhūtasya pate brahmāṇaṃ tyā vṛṇe \\ iti śrutavantam ārṣeyaṃ brahmāṇam̐ vṛṇīte vedikāle 'māvāsyāyām̐ śvobhūte paurṇamāsyām //
5.2.15.d: भूपते भुवनपते महतो भूतस्य पते ब्रह्माणं त्या वृणे \\ इति श्रुतवन्तम् आर्षेयं ब्रह्माणम्̐ वृणीते वेदिकाले ऽमावास्यायाम्̐ श्वोभूते पौर्णमास्याम् //
5.2.15.m: With 'Lord of the earth, lord of the world, lord of great being, I choose thee as brahman priest', he chooses as brahman priest a learned [brahmin] of ṛṣi descent at the time of the vedi, on the new-moon day, or on the full-moon day on the morrow.

5.2.15.s: bhūr bhuvaḥ svar \ deva savitar etaṃ tvā vṛṇate bṛhaspatiṃ brahmāṇam \\ tam ahaṃ manase prabravīmi \ mano vāce \ vāg gāyatryai \ gāyatrī triṣṭubhe \ triṣṭub jagatyai \ jagaty anuṣṭubhe \\ anuṣṭup paṅktaye \ paṅktiḥ prajāpataye \ prajāpatir bṛhaspataye \ bṛhaspatir devānāṃ brahmāhaṃ manuṣyāṇām \\ bṛhaspate yajñaṃ gopāya \\ ahaṃ bhūpatir ahaṃ bhuvanapatir ahaṃ mahato bhūtasya patir aham \\ maho me 'vocas \\ bhargo me 'vocaḥ \ stomaṃ me 'vocas \\ yaśo me 'vocas \\ annādyaṃ me 'vocaḥ \ prajāṃ me 'vocaḥ \ pratiṣṭhāṃ me 'vocas \\ iti vṛto japati /
5.2.15.d: भूर् भुवः स्वर् \ देव सवितर् एतं त्वा वृणते बृहस्पतिं ब्रह्माणम् \\ तम् अहं मनसे प्रब्रवीमि \ मनो वाचे \ वाग् गायत्र्यै \ गायत्री त्रिष्टुभे \ त्रिष्टुब् जगत्यै \ जगत्य् अनुष्टुभे \\ अनुष्टुप् पङ्क्तये \ पङ्क्तिः प्रजापतये \ प्रजापतिर् बृहस्पतये \ बृहस्पतिर् देवानां ब्रह्माहं मनुष्याणाम् \\ बृहस्पते यज्ञं गोपाय \\ अहं भूपतिर् अहं भुवनपतिर् अहं महतो भूतस्य पतिर् अहम् \\ महो मे ऽवोचस् \\ भर्गो मे ऽवोचः \ स्तोमं मे ऽवोचस् \\ यशो मे ऽवोचस् \\ अन्नाद्यं मे ऽवोचः \ प्रजां मे ऽवोचः \ प्रतिष्ठां मे ऽवोचस् \\ इति वृतो जपति /
5.2.15.m: Having been chosen, he mutters: 'Bhūr, bhuvas, svar! O divine Savitṛ, they choose this Bṛhaspati as brahman priest; / him I proclaim to the mind, the mind to speech, speech to the gāyatrī, the gāyatrī to the triṣṭubh, the triṣṭubh to the jagatī, the jagatī to the anuṣṭubh, / the anuṣṭubh to the paṅkti, the paṅkti to Prajāpati, Prajāpati to Bṛhaspati; Bṛhaspati is the brahman priest of the gods, I of men. / O Bṛhaspati, protect the sacrifice! / I am the lord of the earth, I am the lord of the world, I am the lord of great being. / Greatness hast thou spoken for me; splendour hast thou spoken for me; praise hast thou spoken for me; glory hast thou spoken for me; food hast thou spoken for me; offspring hast thou spoken for me; stability hast thou spoken for me.'

5.2.15.s: tīrthenānvety apareṇa vihāraṃ dakṣiṇātikramya yajñopavīty apramatto dakṣiṇata āsīta //
5.2.15.d: तीर्थेनान्वेत्य् अपरेण विहारं दक्षिणातिक्रम्य यज्ञोपवीत्य् अप्रमत्तो दक्षिणत आसीत //
5.2.15.m: Having approached along the ford, having crossed south to the west of the sacrificial enclosure, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, not negligent, he should sit to the south.

5.2.15.s: ahe daidhiṣavyod atas tiṣṭhānyasya sadane sīda yo 'smat pākataras \\ ity āsanam anumantrayeta /
5.2.15.d: अहे दैधिषव्योद् अतस् तिष्ठान्यस्य सदने सीद यो ऽस्मत् पाकतरस् \\ इत्य् आसनम् अनुमन्त्रयेत /
5.2.15.m: With 'O son of a didhiṣū, stand up from here, sit in the seat of another who is simpler than us', he should accompany the seat with the formula.

5.2.15.s: āsanāt tṛṇam ubhayataḥ prachidya nirastaḥ parāvasuḥ saha pāpmanā \\ iti dakṣiṇāpratyak savyena nirasyati //
5.2.15.d: आसनात् तृणम् उभयतः प्रछिद्य निरस्तः परावसुः सह पाप्मना \\ इति दक्षिणाप्रत्यक् सव्येन निरस्यति //
5.2.15.m: Having cut off a blade of grass from both sides from the seat, he casts it towards the south-west with the left hand, with: 'Parāvasu is cast away together with evil.'

5.2.15.s: idam aham arvāgvasoḥ sadane sīdāmi \\ iti dakṣiṇaṃ pādam āsanam abhyantare dadāti tadantareṇa savyam //
5.2.15.d: इदम् अहम् अर्वाग्वसोः सदने सीदामि \\ इति दक्षिणं पादम् आसनम् अभ्यन्तरे ददाति तदन्तरेण सव्यम् //
5.2.15.m: With 'Here I sit in the seat of Arvāgvasu', he places his right foot inside the seat, and after it his left.

5.2.15.s: devena savitrā prasūtas \ tad agnaye prabravīmi \ tad vāyave \ tat sūryāya \\ ity upaviśati //
5.2.15.d: देवेन सवित्रा प्रसूतस् \ तद् अग्नये प्रब्रवीमि \ तद् वायवे \ तत् सूर्याय \\ इत्य् उपविशति //
5.2.15.m: "Impelled by the god Savitṛ, that I announce to Agni, that to Vāyu, that to Sūrya,"—[with this mantra] he sits down.

5.2.15.s: sūryo divo yajñaṃ pātu \ vāyur antarikṣād yajñapatiṃ pātu \\ agnir māṃ pātu mānuṣam iti japati /
5.2.15.d: सूर्यो दिवो यज्ञं पातु \ वायुर् अन्तरिक्षाद् यज्ञपतिं पातु \\ अग्निर् मां पातु मानुषम् इति जपति /
5.2.15.m: "May Sūrya protect the sacrifice from heaven; may Vāyu protect the lord of the sacrifice from the intermediate space; may Agni protect me, the mortal,"—he murmurs [this].

5.2.15.s: brahmaṇy upacaraty anyasya vā karma kurvāṇe yo nediṣṭhī ṛtvijām̐ syāt sa upāsītāpi vā darbhamuṣṭim udapātram̐ vā brahmāsane nyasyed aśūnyāsanam evam̐ syāt //
5.2.15.d: ब्रह्मण्य् उपचरत्य् अन्यस्य वा कर्म कुर्वाणे यो नेदिष्ठी ऋत्विजाम्̐ स्यात् स उपासीतापि वा दर्भमुष्टिम् उदपात्रम्̐ वा ब्रह्मासने न्यस्येद् अशून्यासनम् एवम्̐ स्यात् //
5.2.15.m: When the brahman priest attends to [another ritual task] or performs another's act, whoever among the officiating priests is nearest should sit near [his place]; or he should place a handful of darbha grass or a water vessel on the brahman priest's seat, so that the seat may thus not be empty.

5.2.15.s: brahmann apaḥ praṇeṣyāmi \\ ity ukte praṇaya yajñam \\ devatā vardhaya tvam \\ nākasya pṛṣṭhe svarge loke yajamāno astu // \ saptarṣīṇām̐ sukṛtām̐ yatra lokas \ tatremam̐ yajñam̐ yajamānaṃ ca dhehi // \ bṛhaspatiḥ prasūtas \\ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar \ oṃ praṇaya \\ ity anujānāti /
5.2.15.d: ब्रह्मन्न् अपः प्रणेष्यामि \\ इत्य् उक्ते प्रणय यज्ञम् \\ देवता वर्धय त्वम् \\ नाकस्य पृष्ठे स्वर्गे लोके यजमानो अस्तु // \ सप्तर्षीणाम्̐ सुकृताम्̐ यत्र लोकस् \ तत्रेमम्̐ यज्ञम्̐ यजमानं च धेहि // \ बृहस्पतिः प्रसूतस् \\ भूर् भुवः स्वर् \ ओं प्रणय \\ इत्य् अनुजानाति /
5.2.15.m: When it is said, "O brahman, I shall lead forth the waters," he gives permission: "Lead forth the sacrifice; increase the deities; may the sacrificer be in the heavenly world on the back of the firmament; where the world of the seven sages, the well-doers, is, there place this sacrifice and the sacrificer. Impelled by Bṛhaspati—bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ—oṃ, lead forth!"

5.2.15.s: eṣo 'nujñātaḥ sarvatra yathāmnātam /
5.2.15.d: एषो ऽनुज्ञातः सर्वत्र यथाम्नातम् /
5.2.15.m: This is the form of granting permission everywhere, as traditionally taught.

5.2.15.s: anāmantrito 'nujānāti prokṣantam̐ haviḥ pūrvaṃ parigrāhaṃ parigrahīṣyantam̐ sāmidhenīr anuvakṣyantam /
5.2.15.d: अनामन्त्रितो ऽनुजानाति प्रोक्षन्तम्̐ हविः पूर्वं परिग्राहं परिग्रहीष्यन्तम्̐ सामिधेनीर् अनुवक्ष्यन्तम् /
5.2.15.m: Without being summoned, he grants permission to [the priest] who is sprinkling the oblation, who is about to make the first enclosing outline, and who is about to recite the sāmidhenī verses.

5.2.15.s: pravare cānumantrito 'nyāni mantraprayoge /
5.2.15.d: प्रवरे चानुमन्त्रितो ऽन्यानि मन्त्रप्रयोगे /
5.2.15.m: And in the choosing of the hotṛ priest he is addressed with a mantra, and in other acts at the application of a mantra.

5.2.15.s: vācam̐ yachaty akāle vācam̐ visṛjya vaiṣṇavīṃ nigadya punar yachet //
5.2.15.d: वाचम्̐ यछत्य् अकाले वाचम्̐ विसृज्य वैष्णवीं निगद्य पुनर् यछेत् //
5.2.15.m: He restrains his speech; having released his speech at an improper time, he should recite a Vaiṣṇava verse and restrain it again.

5.2.15.s: ṛtasya pathā paryehi \ mitrasya tvā cakṣuṣānvīkṣe \\ iti prāśitram āhriyamāṇam̐ vīkṣate /
5.2.15.d: ऋतस्य पथा पर्येहि \ मित्रस्य त्वा चक्षुषान्वीक्षे \\ इति प्राशित्रम् आह्रियमाणम्̐ वीक्षते /
5.2.15.m: "Come around by the path of truth; I look upon you with the eye of Mitra,"—[with this mantra] he looks at the prāśitra portion being brought.

5.2.15.s: sāvitreṇa pratigṛhya pṛthivyās tvā pṛṣṭhe sādayāmi \\ iti dakṣiṇato barhiṣi sādayati //
5.2.15.d: सावित्रेण प्रतिगृह्य पृथिव्यास् त्वा पृष्ठे सादयामि \\ इति दक्षिणतो बर्हिषि सादयति //
5.2.15.m: Having received it with the Sāvitra formula, [with] "I set you down on the back of the earth," he sets it down to the south on the sacrificial grass.

5.2.15.s: suparṇasya tvā garutmataś cakṣuṣānvīkṣe \\ ity avekṣate /
5.2.15.d: सुपर्णस्य त्वा गरुत्मतश् चक्षुषान्वीक्षे \\ इत्य् अवेक्षते /
5.2.15.m: "I look upon you with the eye of the fair-winged Garutmat,"—he gazes at it.

5.2.15.s: aṅguṣṭhenopamadhyamayā cādāya \\ agneṣ ṭvāsyena prāśnāmi brāhmaṇasyodareṇa bṛhaspater brahmaṇā \\ indrasya tvā jaṭhare dadhur iti prāśnāty asparśayan dantān //
5.2.15.d: अङ्गुष्ठेनोपमध्यमया चादाय \\ अग्नेष् ट्वास्येन प्राश्नामि ब्राह्मणस्योदरेण बृहस्पतेर् ब्रह्मणा \\ इन्द्रस्य त्वा जठरे दधुर् इति प्राश्नात्य् अस्पर्शयन् दन्तान् //
5.2.15.m: Having taken it with the thumb and the ring finger, [with] "With the mouth of Agni I eat you, with the belly of a brāhmaṇa, with the holy power of Bṛhaspati; they placed you in Indra's stomach," he eats it without letting it touch his teeth.

5.2.15.s: satyena tvābhidhārayāmi \\ ity ācāmati //
5.2.15.d: सत्येन त्वाभिधारयामि \\ इत्य् आचामति //
5.2.15.m: "I moisten you with truth,"—he sips water.

5.2.15.s: vāṅ ma āsye \ nasoḥ prāṇo \ akṣṇoś cakṣuḥ \ karṇayoḥ śrotram \\ bāhvor balam \ ūrvor ojaḥ \ pādayoḥ pratiṣṭhā \\ iti yathāliṅgam aṅgāni saṃmṛśati /
5.2.15.d: वाङ् म आस्ये \ नसोः प्राणो \ अक्ष्णोश् चक्षुः \ कर्णयोः श्रोत्रम् \\ बाह्वोर् बलम् \ ऊर्वोर् ओजः \ पादयोः प्रतिष्ठा \\ इति यथालिङ्गम् अङ्गानि संमृशति /
5.2.15.m: "Speech in my mouth, breath in the nostrils, sight in the eyes, hearing in the ears, strength in the arms, vigor in the thighs, firm foundation in the feet,"—according to their characteristic marks, he touches the limbs.

5.2.15.s: apa upaspṛśya viṣṇor jaṭharam asi \\ iti nābhideśam ārabhya japati \\ ariṣṭā viśvāny aṅgāni \ tanūr me tanvā saha \\ iti gātrāṇi /
5.2.15.d: अप उपस्पृश्य विष्णोर् जठरम् असि \\ इति नाभिदेशम् आरभ्य जपति \\ अरिष्टा विश्वान्य् अङ्गानि \ तनूर् मे तन्वा सह \\ इति गात्राणि /
5.2.15.m: Having touched water, [with] "You are the stomach of Viṣṇu," he murmurs, beginning from the navel region; [and with] "Uninjured be all limbs, my body together with my self," [touching] the limbs.

5.2.15.s: prāśitraharaṇe brahmabhāgam ādadhāti /
5.2.15.d: प्राशित्रहरणे ब्रह्मभागम् आदधाति /
5.2.15.m: He deposits the brahman's share in the prāśitra vessel.

5.2.15.s: śam̐yvante prāśnāty ūrdhvam̐ vā samiṣṭayajuṣaḥ /
5.2.15.d: शम्̐य्वन्ते प्राश्नात्य् ऊर्ध्वम्̐ वा समिष्टयजुषः /
5.2.15.m: He eats it at the end of the śaṃyu formula, or after the samiṣṭayajus offerings.

5.2.15.s: eteneṣṭipaśusomānāṃ brahmatvam̐ vyākhyātam /
5.2.15.d: एतेनेष्टिपशुसोमानां ब्रह्मत्वम्̐ व्याख्यातम् /
5.2.15.m: By this the function of the brahman priest in the iṣṭis, animal sacrifices, and Soma sacrifices has been explained.

5.2.15.s: agnyādheye vṛto brāhmaudanikasya prāśanaṃ kṛtvā vasati /
5.2.15.d: अग्न्याधेये वृतो ब्राह्मौदनिकस्य प्राशनं कृत्वा वसति /
5.2.15.m: In the establishment of the sacred fires, having been chosen, he stays after having performed the eating of the rice meant for brāhmaṇas.

5.2.15.s: śvobhūte saṃbhāraprabhṛtyāvṛto 'dhvaryave /
5.2.15.d: श्वोभूते संभारप्रभृत्यावृतो ऽध्वर्यवे /
5.2.15.m: On the following day, from the bringing of the materials onward, he is [ready] when chosen by the adhvaryu priest.

5.2.15.s: sapatnavato bhrātṛvyavato vā rathacakram̐ vihāre triḥ parivartayet /
5.2.15.d: सपत्नवतो भ्रातृव्यवतो वा रथचक्रम्̐ विहारे त्रिः परिवर्तयेत् /
5.2.15.m: For one having rivals or having an enemy, he should turn a chariot wheel three times in the sacrificial enclosure.

5.2.15.s: varuṇapraghāseṣu vedī kriyamāṇe 'greṇāhavanīyād adhi sphyenānulikhed ā dakṣiṇasyāḥ śroṇer ā pṛṣṭhyāyāḥ śaṅkoḥ some /
5.2.15.d: वरुणप्रघासेषु वेदी क्रियमाणे ऽग्रेणाहवनीयाद् अधि स्फ्येनानुलिखेद् आ दक्षिणस्याः श्रोणेर् आ पृष्ठ्यायाः शङ्कोः सोमे /
5.2.15.m: In the Varuṇapraghāsa rites, when the two altars are being made, he should trace with the wooden sword in front from the āhavanīya fire up to the southern hip and up to the peg of the spine line; [and likewise] in the Soma sacrifice.

5.2.15.s: apratirathenāgnicityāyām /
5.2.15.d: अप्रतिरथेनाग्निचित्यायाम् /
5.2.15.m: In the piling of the fire altar, [he recites] with the Apratiratha hymn.

5.2.15.s: tīrthena niḥsṛtyāvabhṛtham iyāt /
5.2.15.d: तीर्थेन निःसृत्यावभृथम् इयात् /
5.2.15.m: Having gone out by the tīrtha path, he should go to the purificatory bath.

5.2.15.s: pūrṇadarve yady āmantrayeta juhudhi \\ ity anujānīyāt /
5.2.15.d: पूर्णदर्वे यद्य् आमन्त्रयेत जुहुधि \\ इत्य् अनुजानीयात् /
5.2.15.m: At the full-ladle offering, if he is summoned, he should grant permission [saying]: "Offer!"

5.2.15.s: paśubandhe 'pareṇa vihāraṃ dakṣiṇātikramya hutāyām̐ vapāyāṃ cātvāle mārjayitvā /
5.2.15.d: पशुबन्धे ऽपरेण विहारं दक्षिणातिक्रम्य हुतायाम्̐ वपायां चात्वाले मार्जयित्वा /
5.2.15.m: In the animal sacrifice, having crossed to the south behind the sacrificial enclosure, after the omentum has been offered, having cleansed himself at the cātvāla pit,

5.2.15.s: dārśapaurṇamāsikam̐ varaṇam̐ some nivarteta /
5.2.15.d: दार्शपौर्णमासिकम्̐ वरणम्̐ सोमे निवर्तेत /
5.2.15.m: the choice [of priests] belonging to the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices should cease in the Soma sacrifice.

5.2.16.m: He sits attending from the introductory offering onward.
When [the Soma] has been purchased, he approaches eastward together [with the others].
At the end of the gārhapatya fire, he sits attending the cauldron.
When the [materials] are being brought, he walks around.
If uninitiated, he consumes by inhalation.
He follows along the spine line after the vessels of the cauldron.
He follows along after Agni and Soma being led forward.

5.2.16.s: yadi rājānam̐ hared dhavirdhānānte 'dhvaryave pradāyottareṇāgnīdhrīyam apareṇa sado dakṣiṇena sadomārjālīyahavirdhānaṃ gatvājyānāṃ dakṣiṇata udaṅmukha upaviśaty eṣa saṃcaraḥ /
5.2.16.d: यदि राजानम्̐ हरेद् धविर्धानान्ते ऽध्वर्यवे प्रदायोत्तरेणाग्नीध्रीयम् अपरेण सदो दक्षिणेन सदोमार्जालीयहविर्धानं गत्वाज्यानां दक्षिणत उदङ्मुख उपविशत्य् एष संचरः /
5.2.16.m: If he should carry King [Soma], having handed him over to the adhvaryu priest at the rear of the cart-shed, having gone north of the āgnīdhra shed, behind the sadas hut, and south of the sadas hut, the mārjālīya shed, and the cart-shed, he sits down to the south of the clarified butter portions facing north: this is the path of movement.
On the following day, during the animal offering, he sits attending while the clarified butter portions are being scooped.
When they are being brought forward, he walks around.
He sits attending while the cups are being scooped.
Having offered the two drop-offerings, they glide toward the pavamāna stotra.

5.2.16.s: brahman stoṣyāmaḥ praśāstar ity ukte stuta yaśam \\ devatā vardhaya tvam \\ nākasya pṛṣṭhe svarge loke yajamāno astu // \ saptarṣīṇām̐ sukṛtām̐ yatra lokas \ tatremam̐ yajñam̐ yajamānaṃ ca dhatta // \ raśminā kṣayāya kṣayaṃ jinva // \ bṛhaspatiḥ prasūtas \\ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar \ om̐ stuta \\ ity anujānāti /
5.2.16.d: ब्रह्मन् स्तोष्यामः प्रशास्तर् इत्य् उक्ते स्तुत यशम् \\ देवता वर्धय त्वम् \\ नाकस्य पृष्ठे स्वर्गे लोके यजमानो अस्तु // \ सप्तर्षीणाम्̐ सुकृताम्̐ यत्र लोकस् \ तत्रेमम्̐ यज्ञम्̐ यजमानं च धत्त // \ रश्मिना क्षयाय क्षयं जिन्व // \ बृहस्पतिः प्रसूतस् \\ भूर् भुवः स्वर् \ ओम्̐ स्तुत \\ इत्य् अनुजानाति /
5.2.16.m: When it is said, "O brahman, we shall praise; O director!", he grants permission: "Praise glory; increase the deities; may the sacrificer be in the heavenly world on the back of the firmament; where the world of the seven sages, the well-doers, is, there place this sacrifice and the sacrificer. With the ray, quicken the dwelling for the dwelling! Impelled by Bṛhaspati—bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ—oṃ, praise!"

5.2.16.s: etatprabhṛtayas trayastrim̐śat stomabhāgās trayastrim̐śat stotrāṇy aptoryāmṇi / tāny ekaikenānujānāti /
5.2.16.d: एतत्प्रभृतयस् त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शत् स्तोमभागास् त्रयस्त्रिम्̐शत् स्तोत्राण्य् अप्तोर्याम्णि / तान्य् एकैकेनानुजानाति /
5.2.16.m: Beginning with this, there are thirty-three stomabhāga formulas, [corresponding to] thirty-three stotras in the aptoryāma; he grants permission to them one by one.

5.2.16.s: hutāyām̐ vapāyāṃ cātvāle mārjayitvā dhiṣṇyān upasthāyāparayā dvārā sadaḥ praviśyaudumbaryā dakṣiṇata udaṅmukha upaviśaty eṣa saṃcaraḥ /
5.2.16.d: हुतायाम्̐ वपायां चात्वाले मार्जयित्वा धिष्ण्यान् उपस्थायापरया द्वारा सदः प्रविश्यौदुम्बर्या दक्षिणत उदङ्मुख उपविशत्य् एष संचरः /
5.2.16.m: When the omentum has been offered, having cleansed himself at the cātvāla pit, having attended upon the dhiṣṇya hearths, having entered the sadas hut by the western door, he sits down south of the audumbarī post facing north: this is the path of movement.
The path of movement for the consumption by those without dhiṣṇya hearths is to the south of the hotṛ priest's hearth.
At the completion of the pressings, they disperse along the paths of movement for completed rites.
Having gone out by the eastern door, he consumes the parched-grain portions and the Soma portions.
In the piling of the fire altar, [he attends] from the Sāvitra libations onward.

5.2.16.s: nairṛtīś cīyamāne 'gnau dakṣiṇataḥ pakṣasya bahirvedy upāste //
5.2.16.d: नैरृतीश् चीयमाने ऽग्नौ दक्षिणतः पक्षस्य बहिर्वेद्य् उपास्ते //
5.2.16.m: When the fire altar is being piled with the Nairṛta bricks, he sits attending south of the wing, outside the altar.
Urged with "All together!", he restrains his speech.

5.2.16.s: āhutāyām̐ subrahmaṇyāyām̐ vācam̐ visṛjate vācam̐ visṛjate /
5.2.16.d: आहुतायाम्̐ सुब्रह्मण्यायाम्̐ वाचम्̐ विसृजते वाचम्̐ विसृजते /
5.2.16.m: When the Subrahmaṇyā formula has been invoked, he releases his speech, he releases his speech.

6.1.1.s: agniṃ ceṣyamāṇa ukhām̐ saṃbharet paurṇamāsyām amāvāsyāyām ekāṣṭakāyām̐ vā /
6.1.1.d: अग्निं चेष्यमाण उखाम्̐ संभरेत् पौर्णमास्याम् अमावास्यायाम् एकाष्टकायाम्̐ वा /
6.1.1.m: One intending to pile the fire altar should collect [clay for] the ukhā pot on a full-moon day, a new-moon day, or the ekāṣṭakā day.

6.1.1.s: prākṛtīṣu sam̐sthāsu ṣoḍaśivarjam agnim uttaravedyāṃ cinvīta /
6.1.1.d: प्राकृतीषु सम्̐स्थासु षोडशिवर्जम् अग्निम् उत्तरवेद्यां चिन्वीत /
6.1.1.m: In the basic forms of the Soma sacrifice, excluding the ṣoḍaśin, he should pile the fire on the high altar.

6.1.1.s: sāvitranāciketo vānagnir vottaravediṃ cinvītā sattrāhīneṣu /
6.1.1.d: सावित्रनाचिकेतो वानग्निर् वोत्तरवेदिं चिन्वीता सत्त्राहीनेषु /
6.1.1.m: He may pile the Sāvitra or Nāciketa [fire altar], or he may pile the high altar without a fire altar, in sattras and ahīna sacrifices.

6.1.1.s: tūṣṇīṃ juhūm̐ saṃmṛjya sruvam̐ saṃmārṣṭi /
6.1.1.d: तूष्णीं जुहूम्̐ संमृज्य स्रुवम्̐ संमार्ष्टि /
6.1.1.m: Silently having wiped the juhū ladle, he wipes the sruva ladle.

6.1.1.s: juhūm aṣṭagṛhītena pūrayitvā yuñjānaḥ prathamaṃ manas \\ ity aṣṭau nigadyāhutiṃ juhoti /
6.1.1.d: जुहूम् अष्टगृहीतेन पूरयित्वा युञ्जानः प्रथमं मनस् \\ इत्य् अष्टौ निगद्याहुतिं जुहोति /
6.1.1.m: Having filled the juhū ladle with eight portions [of clarified butter], having recited the eight [verses beginning with] "Yoking first the mind...", he offers the oblation.

6.1.1.s: yadi kāmayeta yajñam̐ yajñayaśasenārpayeyam iti deva savitaḥ prasuva yajñam ity etām ūrdhvam̐ yajuṣaḥ kuryāt //
6.1.1.d: यदि कामयेत यज्ञम्̐ यज्ञयशसेनार्पयेयम् इति देव सवितः प्रसुव यज्ञम् इत्य् एताम् ऊर्ध्वम्̐ यजुषः कुर्यात् //
6.1.1.m: If he should desire, "May I unite the sacrifice with the glory of the sacrifice," he should perform [the offering with] this [verse], "O god Savitṛ, impel the sacrifice...", after the yajus formula.

6.1.1.s: ṛcā stomam̐ samardhaya \\ iti caturgṛhītaṃ juhoti /
6.1.1.d: ऋचा स्तोमम्̐ समर्धय \\ इति चतुर्गृहीतं जुहोति /
6.1.1.m: With "Make the stoma complete by the verse...", he offers a fourfold portion.

6.1.1.s: uttarato gārhapatyasya devasya tvā savituḥ prasave \\ ity abhrim ādatte vaiṇavīṃ kalmāṣīm̐ suṣirām ubhayatastīkṣṇām anyatarato vā /
6.1.1.d: उत्तरतो गार्हपत्यस्य देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे \\ इत्य् अभ्रिम् आदत्ते वैणवीं कल्माषीम्̐ सुषिराम् उभयतस्तीक्ष्णाम् अन्यतरतो वा /
6.1.1.m: North of the gārhapatya fire, [reciting] "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ...", he takes the spade, made of bamboo, speckled, hollow, sharp at both ends or at one end.

6.1.1.s: agreṇāhavanīyaṃ pratūrtam̐ vājinn ādrava \\ ity aśvam abhimantrayate yuñjāthām̐ rāsabham iti gardabham //
6.1.1.d: अग्रेणाहवनीयं प्रतूर्तम्̐ वाजिन्न् आद्रव \\ इत्य् अश्वम् अभिमन्त्रयते युञ्जाथाम्̐ रासभम् इति गर्दभम् //
6.1.1.m: To the front of the āhavanīya [fire], he addresses the horse with: 'Quickly, o courser, run forward...' [and] the donkey with: 'Yoke both of you the ass...'.

6.1.1.s: yogeyoge tavastaram ity abhipravrajanty aśvam agrato nayanti //
6.1.1.d: योगेयोगे तवस्तरम् इत्य् अभिप्रव्रजन्त्य् अश्वम् अग्रतो नयन्ति //
6.1.1.m: With 'At every yoke, the stronger...', they set out, leading the horse in front.

6.1.1.s: agniṃ purīṣyam aṅgirasvad ābhara \\ iti japati //
6.1.1.d: अग्निं पुरीष्यम् अङ्गिरस्वद् आभर \\ इति जपति //
6.1.1.m: He mutters: 'Bring the earth-born Agni like the Aṅgirases...'.

6.1.1.s: agniṃ purīṣyam aṅgirasvad achemas \\ iti sametya puruṣam abhimantrayate yasya vājam̐ vivṛñjiṣet /
6.1.1.d: अग्निं पुरीष्यम् अङ्गिरस्वद् अछेमस् \\ इति समेत्य पुरुषम् अभिमन्त्रयते यस्य वाजम्̐ विवृञ्जिषेत् /
6.1.1.m: Coming together, he addresses a person with: 'May we fetch the earth-born Agni like the Aṅgirases...', [the person] whose vigor he wishes to take away.

6.1.1.s: yataḥ sūryasyodayanaṃ tato valmīkavapām apaghnann agniṃ purīṣyam aṅgirasvad bhariṣyāmas \\ iti brūyāt //
6.1.1.d: यतः सूर्यस्योदयनं ततो वल्मीकवपाम् अपघ्नन्न् अग्निं पुरीष्यम् अङ्गिरस्वद् भरिष्यामस् \\ इति ब्रूयात् //
6.1.1.m: Breaking off an anthill mound from where the sun rises, he should say: 'We shall bring the earth-born Agni like the Aṅgirases...'.

6.1.1.s: anv agnir uṣasām agram akśat \\ iti valmīkād abhipravrajanti //
6.1.1.d: अन्व् अग्निर् उषसाम् अग्रम् अक्शत् \\ इति वल्मीकाद् अभिप्रव्रजन्ति //
6.1.1.m: With 'Agni looked upon the vanguard of the dawns...', they set out from the anthill.

6.1.1.s: āgatya vājay adhvānam ity ākhānaṃ prāpya japati //
6.1.1.d: आगत्य वाजय् अध्वानम् इत्य् आखानं प्राप्य जपति //
6.1.1.m: Having arrived, reaching the pit, he mutters: 'Having come, o swift runner, upon the path...'.

6.1.1.s: ākramya vājin \ dyaus te pṛṣṭham iti dvābhyām aśvam ākramayati /
6.1.1.d: आक्रम्य वाजिन् \ द्यौस् ते पृष्ठम् इति द्वाभ्याम् अश्वम् आक्रमयति /
6.1.1.m: With the two [mantras], 'Stepping upon, o courser...' [and] 'Heaven is your back...', he makes the horse step upon [the pit].

6.1.1.s: ākramyamāṇe yajamāno yaṃ dviṣyāt taṃ brūyād amum abhitiṣṭha \\ iti //
6.1.1.d: आक्रम्यमाणे यजमानो यं द्विष्यात् तं ब्रूयाद् अमुम् अभितिष्ठ \\ इति //
6.1.1.m: While [the horse] is stepping upon it, the sacrificer should say about the one he hates: 'Tread upon so-and-so!'.

6.1.1.s: utkrāma \\ ity utkramayati //
6.1.1.d: उत्क्राम \\ इत्य् उत्क्रमयति //
6.1.1.m: With 'Step out!', he makes [the horse] step out.

6.1.1.s: ud akramīt \\ ity aśvam abhimantrayate //
6.1.1.d: उद् अक्रमीत् \\ इत्य् अश्वम् अभिमन्त्रयते //
6.1.1.m: He addresses the horse with: 'He has stepped out...'.

6.1.1.s: ā tvā jigharmi \\ ā viśvataḥ pratyañcam iti dvābhyām aśvapade juhoti //
6.1.1.d: आ त्वा जिघर्मि \\ आ विश्वतः प्रत्यञ्चम् इति द्वाभ्याम् अश्वपदे जुहोति //
6.1.1.m: With the two [mantras], 'I sprinkle you...' [and] 'Hither from all sides facing backward...', he offers into the footprint of the horse.

6.1.1.s: pari vājapatis \ tvam agne dyubhiḥ \ pari tvāgne puram̐ vayam ity ekaikayā parilikhati /
6.1.1.d: परि वाजपतिस् \ त्वम् अग्ने द्युभिः \ परि त्वाग्ने पुरम्̐ वयम् इत्य् एकैकया परिलिखति /
6.1.1.m: With one each [of the mantras], 'The lord of food [has gone] around...', 'You, o Agni, through the days...', [and] 'Around you, o Agni, a fortress we...', he draws a line around.

6.1.1.s: sāvitrair abhrim ādatte caturbhiś chando 'ntaiḥ //
6.1.1.d: सावित्रैर् अभ्रिम् आदत्ते चतुर्भिश् छन्दो ऽन्तैः //
6.1.1.m: He takes the shovel with four Savitṛ formulas ending with meters.

6.1.1.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave \\ ity anuvākaśeṣeṇa khanati //
6.1.1.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे \\ इत्य् अनुवाकशेषेण खनति //
6.1.1.m: With the remainder of the section, 'At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ...', he digs.

6.1.1.s: apām̐ pṛṣṭham asi \\ iti puṣkaraparṇam̐ viveṣṭayati //
6.1.1.d: अपाम्̐ पृष्ठम् असि \\ इति पुष्करपर्णम्̐ विवेष्टयति //
6.1.1.m: With 'You are the back of the waters...', he spreads out a lotus leaf.

6.1.1.s: śarma ca sthaḥ \ sam̐vasethām ity uttarata ākhānasya kṛṣṇājinaṃ puṣkaraparṇaṃ ca sam̐stṛṇāty adhastāt kṛṣṇājinaṃ prāggrīvam uttaralomam upariṣṭānnābhi prāgdvāraṃ puṣkaraparṇam /
6.1.1.d: शर्म च स्थः \ सम्̐वसेथाम् इत्य् उत्तरत आखानस्य कृष्णाजिनं पुष्करपर्णं च सम्̐स्तृणात्य् अधस्तात् कृष्णाजिनं प्राग्ग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमम् उपरिष्टान्नाभि प्राग्द्वारं पुष्करपर्णम् /
6.1.1.m: With 'You two are protection...' [and] 'May you two dwell together...', to the north of the pit, he spreads out a black antelope skin and a lotus leaf: the black antelope skin underneath, with neck toward the east and fur on top; the lotus leaf on top, with its stalk toward the east.

6.1.1.s: tasmin purīṣyo 'si viśvabharās \\ iti yajuṣā purīṣam āvapaty ṛgbhis tisṛbhiś ca tvām agne puṣkarād adhi \ tam u tvā dadhyaṅṅ ṛṣis \ tam u tvā pāthyo vṛṣā \\ iti gāyatrībhir brāhmaṇasyottarābhis triṣṭubbhī rājanyasyottamābhir jagatībhir vaiśyasya /
6.1.1.d: तस्मिन् पुरीष्यो ऽसि विश्वभरास् \\ इति यजुषा पुरीषम् आवपत्य् ऋग्भिस् तिसृभिश् च त्वाम् अग्ने पुष्कराद् अधि \ तम् उ त्वा दध्यङ्ङ् ऋषिस् \ तम् उ त्वा पाथ्यो वृषा \\ इति गायत्रीभिर् ब्राह्मणस्योत्तराभिस् त्रिष्टुब्भी राजन्यस्योत्तमाभिर् जगतीभिर् वैश्यस्य /
6.1.1.m: Upon it, he pours the earth with the yajus: 'Earth-born are you, all-bearing...'; and with three ṛcs: 'You, o Agni, from the lotus...' 'Him indeed [the sage] Dadhyac...' [and] 'Him indeed the manly Pāthya...': with gāyatrī [verses] for a brāhmaṇa, with the following triṣṭubh [verses] for a rājanya, [and] with the final jagatī [verses] for a vaiśya.

6.1.1.s: yaṃ kāmayetardhnuyād iti tasya gāyatrībhiś ca triṣṭubbhiś ca saṃbhared gāyatryābhyādāya triṣṭubhā nivapati //
6.1.1.d: यं कामयेतर्ध्नुयाद् इति तस्य गायत्रीभिश् च त्रिष्टुब्भिश् च संभरेद् गायत्र्याभ्यादाय त्रिष्टुभा निवपति //
6.1.1.m: For one whom he wishes 'May he prosper', he should gather [the earth] with both gāyatrīs and triṣṭubhs: taking it up with a gāyatrī, he pours it out with a triṣṭubh.

6.1.1.s: ayaṃ te yonir ṛtviyas \\ iti nyuptam abhimṛśati //
6.1.1.d: अयं ते योनिर् ऋत्वियस् \\ इति न्युप्तम् अभिमृशति //
6.1.1.m: With 'This is your seasonal womb...', he touches what has been poured out.

6.1.1.s: apo devīḥ \ saṃ te vāyur ity adbhir ākhānam upasṛjati /
6.1.1.d: अपो देवीः \ सं ते वायुर् इत्य् अद्भिर् आखानम् उपसृजति /
6.1.1.m: With 'O divine waters...' [and] 'May Vāyu [accord] with you...', he pours water onto the pit.

6.1.1.s: sujāto jyotiṣā \\ iti purīṣam abhimantrayate //
6.1.1.d: सुजातो ज्योतिषा \\ इति पुरीषम् अभिमन्त्रयते //
6.1.1.m: He addresses the earth with: 'Well born with light...'.

6.1.1.s: vāso agne viśvarūpam ity upanahyati mauñjena dāmnārkamayeṇa vā //
6.1.1.d: वासो अग्ने विश्वरूपम् इत्य् उपनह्यति मौञ्जेन दाम्नार्कमयेण वा //
6.1.1.m: With 'A garment of all colors, o Agni...', he ties it up with a cord of muñja grass or made of arka [fiber].

6.1.1.s: ud u tiṣṭha svadhvara \\ ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇas \\ ity ādāyottiṣṭhati //
6.1.1.d: उद् उ तिष्ठ स्वध्वर \\ ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु णस् \\ इत्य् आदायोत्तिष्ठति //
6.1.1.m: With 'Stand up, o you of good sacrifice...' [and] 'Upright unto us...', he takes it and stands up.

6.1.1.s: sa jāto garbho asi rodasyor iti japati //
6.1.1.d: स जातो गर्भो असि रोदस्योर् इति जपति //
6.1.1.m: He mutters: 'Born, you are the embryo of both heaven and earth...'.

6.1.1.s: sthiro bhava vīḍvaṅgas \\ iti gardabha ādadhāti //
6.1.1.d: स्थिरो भव वीड्वङ्गस् \\ इति गर्दभ आदधाति //
6.1.1.m: With 'Be firm, strong-limbed...', he places it on the donkey.

6.1.1.s: śivo bhava prajābhyas \\ iti purīṣam abhimantrayate /
6.1.1.d: शिवो भव प्रजाभ्यस् \\ इति पुरीषम् अभिमन्त्रयते /
6.1.1.m: He addresses the earth with: 'Be auspicious for the creatures...'.

6.1.1.s: aśvaprathamāḥ pratyāyanti //
6.1.1.d: अश्वप्रथमाः प्रत्यायन्ति //
6.1.1.m: They return with the horse in front.

6.1.1.s: praitu vājī \\ ity aśvam abhimantrayate nānadad rāsabhaḥ patvā \\ iti gardabham agna āyāhi vītaye \\ iti purīṣam //
6.1.1.d: प्रैतु वाजी \\ इत्य् अश्वम् अभिमन्त्रयते नानदद् रासभः पत्वा \\ इति गर्दभम् अग्न आयाहि वीतये \\ इति पुरीषम् //
6.1.1.m: He addresses the horse with: 'Let the courser advance...', the donkey with: 'Loudly braying, flying ass...', [and] the earth with: 'O Agni, come to the banquet...'

6.1.1.s: ṛtam̐ satyam ṛtam̐ satyam iti puruṣam̐ yena saṃgacheta tam abhimantrayeta /
6.1.1.d: ऋतम्̐ सत्यम् ऋतम्̐ सत्यम् इति पुरुषम्̐ येन संगछेत तम् अभिमन्त्रयेत /
6.1.1.m: With 'The right, the true! The right, the true!', he should address whatever person he encounters.

6.1.1.s: dakṣiṇata āhavanīyasya kharaṃ kṛtvā pariśrayati /
6.1.1.d: दक्षिणत आहवनीयस्य खरं कृत्वा परिश्रयति /
6.1.1.m: Having made a mound to the south of the āhavanīya [fire], he encloses it.

6.1.1.s: tasmin darbhān āstīrya \\ oṣadhayaḥ pratigṛbhṇīta \\ iti dvābhyāṃ khare sādayati /
6.1.1.d: तस्मिन् दर्भान् आस्तीर्य \\ ओषधयः प्रतिगृभ्णीत \\ इति द्वाभ्यां खरे सादयति /
6.1.1.m: Having strewn darbha grass on it, he sets [the earth] down on the mound with the two [mantras]: 'O plants, receive...'

6.1.1.s: aśvagardabhāv adhvaryave dadāti /
6.1.1.d: अश्वगर्दभाव् अध्वर्यवे ददाति /
6.1.1.m: He gives the horse and the donkey to the adhvaryu.

6.1.2.s: vi pājasā \\ iti dvābhyām̐ viṣyati /
6.1.2.d: वि पाजसा \\ इति द्वाभ्याम्̐ विष्यति /
6.1.2.m: With the two [mantras], 'With strength...', he unties [the bundle].

6.1.2.s: parṇavalkalaphāṇṭābhir adbhir āpo hi ṣṭhā \\ iti tisṛbhir upasṛjati //
6.1.2.d: पर्णवल्कलफाण्टाभिर् अद्भिर् आपो हि ष्ठा \\ इति तिसृभिर् उपसृजति //
6.1.2.m: With water decocted with the bark of a palāśa tree, he moistens [the earth] with the three [verses]: 'Since you are waters, refreshing...'.

6.1.2.s: mitraḥ sam̐sṛjya \\ iti dvābhyāṃ pañcabhiḥ saṃbhāraiḥ sam̐sṛjaty ajalomabhiḥ kṛṣṇājinasya tribhiś cūrṇīkṛtaiḥ śarkarābhir veṇvaṅgārair armakapālaiḥ sikatābhiś ca //
6.1.2.d: मित्रः सम्̐सृज्य \\ इति द्वाभ्यां पञ्चभिः संभारैः सम्̐सृजत्य् अजलोमभिः कृष्णाजिनस्य त्रिभिश् चूर्णीकृतैः शर्कराभिर् वेण्वङ्गारैर् अर्मकपालैः सिकताभिश् च //
6.1.2.m: With the two [mantras], 'Mitra, having mixed...', he mixes [the earth] with five ingredients: goat hair, three parts of black antelope skin reduced to powder, gravel, bamboo charcoal, potsherds from an old settlement, and sand.

6.1.2.s: sam̐sṛṣṭām̐ vasubhir iti tisṛbhir abhimantrya patnyai prayachati //
6.1.2.d: सम्̐सृष्टाम्̐ वसुभिर् इति तिसृभिर् अभिमन्त्र्य पत्न्यै प्रयछति //
6.1.2.m: Having addressed [the lump of clay] with the three [mantras], 'Mixed by the Vasus...', he hands it to the wife.

6.1.2.s: makhasya śiro 'si \\ iti piṇḍam abhimṛśati /
6.1.2.d: मखस्य शिरो ऽसि \\ इति पिण्डम् अभिमृशति /
6.1.2.m: With 'You are the head of Makha...', he touches the lump.

6.1.2.s: patny ukhāṃ karoti tryuddhiṃ caturaśrām /
6.1.2.d: पत्न्य् उखां करोति त्र्युद्धिं चतुरश्राम् /
6.1.2.m: The wife makes the ukhā pot, four-cornered and with three belts.

6.1.2.s: āsnātaṃ pramāṇaṃ prathayitvā tām̐ samunnīyoddhīr madhya ādadhāti /
6.1.2.d: आस्नातं प्रमाणं प्रथयित्वा ताम्̐ समुन्नीयोद्धीर् मध्य आदधाति /
6.1.2.m: Having spread [the clay] to the measure of a span, and having raised it up, she places belts in the middle.

6.1.2.s: kriyamāṇām̐ yajamāno 'numantrayate vasavas tvā kṛṇvantu \\ iti prathamām uddhim \\ rudrās tvā \\ iti dvitīyām ādityās tvā \\ iti tṛtīyām \\ viśve tvā devā vaiśvānarāḥ kṛṇvantu \\ iiti sam̐lipyamānāṃ dhruvāprabhṛtibhiḥ /
6.1.2.d: क्रियमाणाम्̐ यजमानो ऽनुमन्त्रयते वसवस् त्वा कृण्वन्तु \\ इति प्रथमाम् उद्धिम् \\ रुद्रास् त्वा \\ इति द्वितीयाम् आदित्यास् त्वा \\ इति तृतीयाम् \\ विश्वे त्वा देवा वैश्वानराः कृण्वन्तु \\ इइति सम्̐लिप्यमानां ध्रुवाप्रभृतिभिः /
6.1.2.m: While it is being made, the sacrificer accompanies [the action] with the mantras: 'May the Vasus make you...' for the first belt; 'May the Rudras make you...' for the second; 'May the Ādityas make you...' for the third; [and] 'May the All-Gods Vaiśvānarās make you...' as it is being smeared around, with [the verses] beginning with Dhruvā.

6.1.2.s: patnī dvyaṅgule 'dhastād dvārasya \\ adityā rāsnāsi \\ iti rāsnāṃ karoti //
6.1.2.d: पत्नी द्व्यङ्गुले ऽधस्ताद् द्वारस्य \\ अदित्या रास्नासि \\ इति रास्नां करोति //
6.1.2.m: Two fingers below the rim, the wife makes a girdle with: 'You are Aditi's girdle...'.

6.1.2.s: aditiṣ ṭe bilam iti dvāram̐ rāsnāyāḥ /
6.1.2.d: अदितिष् टे बिलम् इति द्वारम्̐ रास्नायाः /
6.1.2.m: With 'Aditi is your opening...', [she forms] the opening of the girdle.

6.1.2.s: dikṣu dvau caturo 'ṣṭau vā stanān karoti /
6.1.2.d: दिक्षु द्वौ चतुरो ऽष्टौ वा स्तनान् करोति /
6.1.2.m: In the cardinal directions, she makes two, four, or eight nipples.

6.1.2.s: ikṣuśalākayā nilipya kṛtvāya sā mahīm ukhām iti viṣajati /
6.1.2.d: इक्षुशलाकया निलिप्य कृत्वाय सा महीम् उखाम् इति विषजति /
6.1.2.m: Having smoothed [it] with a reed stalk, she fastens it [for drying] with: 'Having made this great ukhā pot...'.

6.1.2.s: śeṣasya tryālikhitām aṣāḍhām iṣṭakāṃ karoti //
6.1.2.d: शेषस्य त्र्यालिखिताम् अषाढाम् इष्टकां करोति //
6.1.2.m: From the remainder [of the clay], she makes the aṣāḍhā brick, marked with three lines.

6.1.2.s: vasavas tvā dhūpayantu \\ itiprabhṛtibhir gārhapatyād aśvaśakena kharadeśe dhūpayati /
6.1.2.d: वसवस् त्वा धूपयन्तु \\ इतिप्रभृतिभिर् गार्हपत्याद् अश्वशकेन खरदेशे धूपयति /
6.1.2.m: With [the formulas] beginning with 'May the Vasus fumigate you...', he fumigates it at the place of the mound with horse dung from the gārhapatya [fire].

6.1.2.s: agreṇa gārhapatyam aditiṣ ṭvā devī \\ ity āpākaṃ khanati //
6.1.2.d: अग्रेण गार्हपत्यम् अदितिष् ट्वा देवी \\ इत्य् आपाकं खनति //
6.1.2.m: In front of the gārhapatya [fire], with 'May the goddess Aditi...', he digs a baking pit.

6.1.2.s: devānāṃ tvā patnīr ity ukhām ādhāyāṣāḍhām ādadhāti /
6.1.2.d: देवानां त्वा पत्नीर् इत्य् उखाम् आधायाषाढाम् आदधाति /
6.1.2.m: With 'May the wives of the gods...', having placed the ukhā pot [in the pit], he places the aṣāḍhā [brick].

6.1.2.s: kupinaiḥ pariśritya pacanam abhyudya dhiṣaṇā tvā devī \\ itiprabhṛtibhir gārhapatyāt pacati //
6.1.2.d: कुपिनैः परिश्रित्य पचनम् अभ्युद्य धिषणा त्वा देवी \\ इतिप्रभृतिभिर् गार्हपत्यात् पचति //
6.1.2.m: Having enclosed it with mats and piled up fuel, he bakes [them] with [fuel from] the gārhapatya [fire], with [the mantras] beginning with 'May the divine Dhiṣaṇā...'.

6.1.2.s: mitrasya carṣaṇīdhṛtas \\ ity abhīddhām upacarati //
6.1.2.d: मित्रस्य चर्षणीधृतस् \\ इत्य् अभीद्धाम् उपचरति //
6.1.2.m: With 'Of Mitra, supporter of men...', he attends to [the pot] when it is fully ignited.

6.1.2.s: devas tvā savitodvapatu \\ iti pakvām udvapati //
6.1.2.d: देवस् त्वा सवितोद्वपतु \\ इति पक्वाम् उद्वपति //
6.1.2.m: With 'May the divine Savitṛ remove you...', he removes [the pot] when baked.

6.1.2.s: uttiṣṭha bṛhatī bhava \\ ity ādāyottiṣṭhati /
6.1.2.d: उत्तिष्ठ बृहती भव \\ इत्य् आदायोत्तिष्ठति /
6.1.2.m: With 'Stand up, become great...', he takes [it] and stands up.

6.1.2.s: agreṇāhavanīyaṃ paryāhṛtya khare nidhāya mitraitāṃ ta ukhāṃ paridadāmi \\ iti mitrāya paridadāti /
6.1.2.d: अग्रेणाहवनीयं पर्याहृत्य खरे निधाय मित्रैतां त उखां परिददामि \\ इति मित्राय परिददाति /
6.1.2.m: Having carried [it] around in front of the āhavanīya [fire] and set [it] down on the mound, he entrusts [it] to Mitra with: 'O Mitra, I entrust this ukhā pot to you!'.

6.1.2.s: taptām ajakṣīreṇa vasavas tvāchṛndantu \\ itiprabhṛtibhiś caturbhir āchṛṇatti /
6.1.2.d: तप्ताम् अजक्षीरेण वसवस् त्वाछृन्दन्तु \\ इतिप्रभृतिभिश् चतुर्भिर् आछृणत्ति /
6.1.2.m: While it is hot, he sprinkles it with goat milk using the four [formulas] beginning with: 'May the Vasus sprinkle you...'.

6.1.2.s: śiraś chittvāharati vaiśyasya rājanyabandhor vāśanihatasyeṣuhatasya vā /
6.1.2.d: शिरश् छित्त्वाहरति वैश्यस्य राजन्यबन्धोर् वाशनिहतस्येषुहतस्य वा /
6.1.2.m: Having cut off the head of a vaiśya or a rājanya-relative who was struck by lightning or struck by an arrow, he brings it.

6.1.2.s:
ayam̐ yo asya yasya ta idam̐ śiras \\ etena tvam̐ śīrṣaṇyām edhi /
iti chede 'pinidadhāti saptadhā vidīrṇām̐ valmīkavapām̐ sapta ca māṣān /
6.1.2.d:
अयम्̐ यो अस्य यस्य त इदम्̐ शिरस् \\ एतेन त्वम्̐ शीर्षण्याम् एधि /
इति छेदे ऽपिनिदधाति सप्तधा विदीर्णाम्̐ वल्मीकवपाम्̐ सप्त च माषान् /
6.1.2.m: With 'This one who of him, whose this head is... / By this be you having a head!', / he inserts into the cut an anthill mound split in seven parts and seven beans.

6.1.2.s:
idam asmākaṃ bhuje bhogāya bhūyāsam //
iti śiraḥ pāṇau kurute /
6.1.2.d:
इदम् अस्माकं भुजे भोगाय भूयासम् //
इति शिरः पाणौ कुरुते /
6.1.2.m: With 'May this be for our enjoyment and use!', / he takes the head into his hands.

6.1.2.s:
yo 'sya kauṣṭhya jagataḥ \ pārthivasyaiva id vaśī /
yamaṃ bhaṅgaśravo gāya \ yo rājānaparodhyaḥ //
yamaṃ gāya bhaṅgaśravas\ yo rājānaparodhyaḥ /
yenāpo nadyo dhanvāni \ yena dyauḥ pṛthivī dṛḍhā //
hiraṇyakeśān sudhurān \ hiraṇyākṣān ayaḥśaphān /
aśvān anaśvato dānam\ yamo rājādhitiṣṭhati //
aharahar nayamānas\ gā aśvān puruṣān paśūn /
vaivasvato na tṛpyati \ surayā iva durmadaḥ //
iti yamagāthā gāyañ śira āhṛtya mṛdā pralimpati /
6.1.2.d:
यो ऽस्य कौष्ठ्य जगतः \ पार्थिवस्यैव इद् वशी /
यमं भङ्गश्रवो गाय \ यो राजानपरोध्यः //
यमं गाय भङ्गश्रवस्\ यो राजानपरोध्यः /
येनापो नद्यो धन्वानि \ येन द्यौः पृथिवी दृढा //
हिरण्यकेशान् सुधुरान् \ हिरण्याक्षान् अयःशफान् /
अश्वान् अनश्वतो दानम्\ यमो राजाधितिष्ठति //
अहरहर् नयमानस्\ गा अश्वान् पुरुषान् पशून् /
वैवस्वतो न तृप्यति \ सुरया इव दुर्मदः //
इति यमगाथा गायञ् शिर आहृत्य मृदा प्रलिम्पति /
6.1.2.m:
'He who is contained within this world, / who alone has power over what is earthly,'

'Sing of Yama, the glorious breaker, / who is the irresistible king.'

"Sing to Yama, O Bhaṅgaśravas, to the king who cannot be warded off,

by whom the waters, rivers, deserts, by whom heaven and earth are made firm,

golden-haired, well-yoked, golden-eyed, iron-hoofed,

horses—to the horseless the gift—King Yama presides [over them].

Day by day leading away cows, horses, men, beasts,

the son of Vivasvant is not satiated, like one madly drunk with surā."

Singing these verses to Yama, having fetched the [human] head, he smears it with clay.

6.1.3.s: pañca sāṇḍān ālabhate prājāpatyam ajam agnibhyaḥ kāmebhyo 'śvam ṛṣabham̐ vṛṣṇiṃ bastam /
6.1.3.d: पञ्च साण्डान् आलभते प्राजापत्यम् अजम् अग्निभ्यः कामेभ्यो ऽश्वम् ऋषभम्̐ वृष्णिं बस्तम् /
6.1.3.m: He immolates five uncastrated animals: a goat for Prajāpati, a horse, a bull, a ram, and a he-goat for the Agnis desiring [oblations].
The ritual is established up to the kindling verses.

6.1.3.s: anabhyāvartayam̐ś caturvim̐śatim̐ sāmidhenīr anvāha pra vo vājā abhidyavas \\ ity ekādaśa samās tvāgna ṛtavo vardhayantu \\ iti daśa / jyotiṣmatīṃ parihāyāprīr uttamā upem asṛkṣi \\ ity apsumatīs tisro jyotiṣmatyā paridadhāti /
6.1.3.d: अनभ्यावर्तयम्̐श् चतुर्विम्̐शतिम्̐ सामिधेनीर् अन्वाह प्र वो वाजा अभिद्यवस् \\ इत्य् एकादश समास् त्वाग्न ऋतवो वर्धयन्तु \\ इति दश / ज्योतिष्मतीं परिहायाप्रीर् उत्तमा उपेम् असृक्षि \\ इत्य् अप्सुमतीस् तिस्रो ज्योतिष्मत्या परिदधाति /
6.1.3.m: Without repetition he recites twenty-four kindling verses: eleven with "Forth your waters, bright...", ten with "May the seasons increase you for years, O Agni..."; having omitted the verse containing the word jyotis, the last of the Āprī verses, he encloses with three verses containing the word ap, beginning with "I have sent forth...", [and] with the one containing the word jyotis.
With "The golden germ..." he pours the ladle-pouring of clarified butter.
The ritual is established up to the carrying of fire around [the victims].

6.1.3.s: uttaraṃ prājāpatyaṃ nidhāya śiro triḥ paryagniṃ karoti /
