He drives a chariot outside the vedi.

7.2.2.s: aharahar yogavimokānvārambhānvārohāpsumatyāvahasaṃtānāś ca vasatīvarīr idhmābarhiḥ payasāṃ dohanam /
7.2.2.d: अहरहर् योगविमोकान्वारम्भान्वारोहाप्सुमत्यावहसंतानाश् च वसतीवरीर् इध्माबर्हिः पयसां दोहनम् /
7.2.2.m: Day after day occur the yoking and unyoking [of the fires], the holding on, the mounting, the two apsumatī verses, the continuous performance of the day rites, the vasatīvarī waters, the sacrificial fuel and grass, and the milking of the milks.
From here on, he announces to the āgnīdhra the pressing of tomorrow.
The [second day] is an ukthya having the fifteenfold stoma, with the Bṛhat as its sāman.

7.2.2.s: dundubhiśabdena stotram upākaroti yadi na stanayet /
7.2.2.d: दुन्दुभिशब्देन स्तोत्रम् उपाकरोति यदि न स्तनयेत् /
7.2.2.m: He brings near the stotra with the sound of a drum, if it does not thunder.
The [third day] is an ukthya having the seventeenfold stoma, with the Vairūpa as its sāman.
He brings near the stotra with fanning.
The rule for the atigrāhya cups is as in the Vājapeya.
The [fourth day] is a ṣoḍaśin having the twenty-onefold stoma, with the Vairāja as its sāman.

7.2.2.s: agna āyūm̐ṣi pavase \\ ity āgneyam atigrāhyaṃ gṛhṇāti \\ agneś ca tvā brahmaṇaś ca tejasā juhomi \\ iti juhoti \\ agna āyuḥkāra \\ iti bhakṣayataḥ /
7.2.2.d: अग्न आयूम्̐षि पवसे \\ इत्य् आग्नेयम् अतिग्राह्यं गृह्णाति \\ अग्नेश् च त्वा ब्रह्मणश् च तेजसा जुहोमि \\ इति जुहोति \\ अग्न आयुःकार \\ इति भक्षयतः /
7.2.2.m: He draws the atigrāhya cup for Agni with: “O Agni, you purify life-breaths…”. He offers it with: “And with the brilliance of Agni and of the brahman I offer you.” With: “O Agni, life-maker…”, the two partake of it.
He brings near the stotra with the two fire-churning sticks.
Having spread avakā plants, he churns fire on the udgātṛ’s thigh.

7.2.2.s: tam adhvaryur bhavataṃ naḥ samanasau \\ ity āhavanīye hutvā preddho agne \\ iti virājābhijuhoti /
7.2.2.d: तम् अध्वर्युर् भवतं नः समनसौ \\ इत्य् आहवनीये हुत्वा प्रेद्धो अग्ने \\ इति विराजाभिजुहोति /
7.2.2.m: The adhvaryu, having offered it into the āhavanīya fire with: “Be of one mind for us…”, makes an additional offering with the Virāj verse: “Kindled, O Agni…”
The [fifth day] is an ukthya having the thrice-ninefold stoma, with the Śākvara as its sāman.

7.2.2.s: ojas tad asya titviṣe \\ ity aindram atigrāhyaṃ gṛhṇāti \\ indrasya ca tvā kṣatrasya caujasā juhomi \\ iti juhoti \\ indraujaskāra \\ iti bhakṣayataḥ /
7.2.2.d: ओजस् तद् अस्य तित्विषे \\ इत्य् ऐन्द्रम् अतिग्राह्यं गृह्णाति \\ इन्द्रस्य च त्वा क्षत्रस्य चौजसा जुहोमि \\ इति जुहोति \\ इन्द्रौजस्कार \\ इति भक्षयतः /
7.2.2.m: He draws the atigrāhya cup for Indra with: “His vigor shone brightly…”. He offers it with: “And with the vigor of Indra and of the kṣatra I offer you.” With: “O Indra, vigor-maker…”, the two partake of it.
He brings near the stotra with water containing avakā plants.
While they make the waters splash, they chant the stotra.
When it is completed, they pour [the waters] out at the mārjālīya hearth.
The [sixth day] is an ukthya having the thirty-threefold stoma, with the Raivata as its sāman.

7.2.2.s: adṛśrann asya ketavas \\ iti sauryam atigrāhyaṃ gṛhṇāti sūryasya ca tvauṣadhīnāṃ ca varcasā juhomi \\ iti juhoti sūrya bhrājaskāra \\ iti bhakṣayataḥ /
7.2.2.d: अदृश्रन्न् अस्य केतवस् \\ इति सौर्यम् अतिग्राह्यं गृह्णाति सूर्यस्य च त्वौषधीनां च वर्चसा जुहोमि \\ इति जुहोति सूर्य भ्राजस्कार \\ इति भक्षयतः /
7.2.2.m: He draws the atigrāhya cup for Sūrya with: “His beacons have become visible…”. He offers it with: “And with the radiance of Sūrya and of the herbs I offer you.” With: “O Sūrya, radiance-maker…”, the two partake of it.
The sixth day has its own season-formula.
He joins the offering verse to the ritual call:

7.2.2.s:
ye3 yajāmahe \\ aśvinādhvaryū ādhvaryavāt \\ ṛtunā somaṃ pibatam
aśvinā pibataṃ madhu \ dīdyagnī śucivratā / \ ṛtunā yajñavāhasā //
iti samūḍhe /
7.2.2.d:
ये3 यजामहे \\ अश्विनाध्वर्यू आध्वर्यवात् \\ ऋतुना सोमं पिबतम्
अश्विना पिबतं मधु \ दीद्यग्नी शुचिव्रता / \ ऋतुना यज्ञवाहसा //
इति समूढे /
7.2.2.m:
“We who sacrifice… / O two Aśvins, adhvaryus, from the adhvaryu’s office, / drink the soma in due season!”

“O Aśvins, drink the sweet [draft], / you whose fires shine, whose vows are pure, / who convey the sacrifice in due season!”

7.2.2.s:
arvāñcam adya yayyaṃ nṛvāhaṇam\ ratham̐ yuñjāthām iha vām̐ vimocanam /
pṛṅktam̐ havīm̐ṣi madhunā hi kaṃ gatam \ athā somaṃ pibatam̐ vājinīvasū //
iti vyūḍhe //
7.2.2.d:
अर्वाञ्चम् अद्य यय्यं नृवाहणम्\ रथम्̐ युञ्जाथाम् इह वाम्̐ विमोचनम् /
पृङ्क्तम्̐ हवीम्̐षि मधुना हि कं गतम् \ अथा सोमं पिबतम्̐ वाजिनीवसू //
इति व्यूढे //
7.2.2.m:
“Yoke today the chariot directed toward us, which is to be driven, conveying men; / here is your unyoking.

Mix the oblations with honey, for you have arrived; / then drink the soma, O rich in horses!”
[The formula beginning:] “Agni, lord of the house, from the gārhapatya fire…” is used in the samūḍha arrangement.
In the vyūḍha arrangement, another triṣṭubh verse is handed down.
He brings near the stotra with the lowing of cows.
At the third pressing, the ritual craft is the response in the ukthya rites.
The maitrāvaruṇa arranges the Vālakhilya hymns separately.
The brāhmaṇācchaṃsin recites the Vṛṣākapi hymn; the acchāvāka recites the Evayāmarut hymn.

7.2.2.s: ṣaḍahe sam̐sthite madhv aśnanti ghṛtam̐ vā /
7.2.2.d: षडहे सम्̐स्थिते मध्व् अश्नन्ति घृतम्̐ वा /
7.2.2.m: When the six-day period is completed, they eat honey or clarified butter.

7.2.2.d: उक्थ्याश् छन्दोमास् तायन्ते चतुर्विम्̐शश् चतुश्चत्वारिम्̐शो ऽष्टाचत्वारिम्̐शः /
7.2.2.m: The chandoma days are performed as ukthyas: the twenty-fourfold, forty-fourfold, and forty-eightfold.
